children.top_down_role: Stability of graphical difference quotients and tangent models.

children.title: Proto-Differentiability
children.top_down_role: Stability of graphical difference-quotient limits.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) when its graphical difference quotients converge to \(DF(\bar x,\bar y)\).

notation.meaning: graph of the set-valued mapping F
graphical derivative of F at the reference graph point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional graphical definition via difference-quotient convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), define the graphical difference quotient \(F_t:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) by
\[
F_t(u):=\frac{F(\bar x+tu)-\bar y}{t}.
\]
The mapping \(F\) is proto-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar y\) if the sets \(\operatorname{gph}F_t\) converge as \(t\downarrow0\) in the Painleve-Kuratowski sense. Their limit must then equal
\[
\operatorname{gph}DF(\bar x,\bar y)=T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y),
\]
where \(T\) is the contingent tangent cone. Thus proto-differentiability requires equality of the inner and outer graphical limits, not merely existence of tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proto-differentiability means that rescaled graphs about a reference graph point converge to the graph of the graphical derivative, equivalently to the graph’s tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Proto-Differentiability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graphical-limit formulation is plausible, but proto-differentiability has convention-sensitive formulations and no source or locator is supplied to verify the precise convergence requirement and identification of the limit.

children.title: Graphical Regularity
children.top_down_role: Regularity of tangent models for set-valued graphs.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graphical regularity holds exactly when \(\widehat N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)=N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone regularity of a locally closed graph at a reference point.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.4 Graphical Regularity of Lipschitzian Mappings p. 327
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(F\) is graphically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) when its graph is normally regular there, namely
\[
\widehat N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)=N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y).
\]
Here the left-hand side is the Frechet regular normal cone and the right-hand side is the limiting normal cone. Since \(\widehat N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\subseteq N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\) always holds for a locally closed graph, graphical regularity excludes additional limiting normals arising only from nearby graph points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is graphically regular at a graph point when the regular and limiting normal cones to its graph coincide there.
knowledge_statements.title: Graphical Regularity

children.title: Proto-Differentiability–Regularity Interface
children.top_down_role: Regimes linking quotient stability to regular graphical geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) has locally closed graph and is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
\(F\) is graphically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coderivative is recovered by polarity from the graph of the proto-derivative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-normal polarity connecting proto-derivatives and coderivatives under graphical regularity.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.4 Graphical Regularity of Lipschitzian Mappings p. 327
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Proto-differentiability identifies the tangent geometry by
\[
\operatorname{gph}DF(\bar x,\bar y)=T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y).
\]
Graphical regularity identifies the limiting normal cone with the polar of that tangent cone. Consequently, for every \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\),
\[
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)
=\{x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n:(x^*,-y^*)\in[\operatorname{gph}DF(\bar x,\bar y)]^\circ\}.
\]
Thus the primal first-order graph limit and the dual coderivative are linked by tangent-normal polarity under the two stated regularity hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When proto-differentiability and graphical regularity both hold, the graphical derivative gives the tangent cone and its polar determines the coderivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Proto-Differentiability–Regularity Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Graphical Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative–coderivative characterizations at a locally closed graph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\bar u\in S(\bar x)$ and suppose $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed at $(\bar x,\bar u)$. The following are equivalent: (a) $S$ is graphically regular at $\bar x$ for $\bar u$; (b) $\langle v,w\rangle\leq\langle y,z\rangle$ whenever $v\in D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)(y)$ and $z\in DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)(w)$; (c) $D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)=DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{*+}$; (d) $DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)=D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)^{*-}$; (e) $DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)=\widehat DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)$; and (f) $D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)=\widehat D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)$. Under these equivalent conditions, $DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)$ and $D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)$ are graph-convex and hence sublinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a locally closed graph point, graphical regularity is equivalent to the stated primal-dual inequality, the two derivative–coderivative adjoint identities, and equality of the ordinary and regular graphical derivatives and coderivatives. These conditions also make the graphical derivative and coderivative graph-convex and therefore sublinear.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed at }(\bar x,\bar u)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conditions (a)--(f) are equivalent, and each implies that }DS(\bar x\mid\bar u)\text{ and }D^*S(\bar x\mid\bar u)\text{ are graph-convex and sublinear.}

children.title: Coderivative Scalarization
children.top_down_role: Reduction of dual mapping differentiation to scalarized subdifferentials.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is single-valued and strictly Lipschitzian at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*f(\bar x)(y^*)=\partial\langle y^*,f\rangle(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-coderivative scalarization for a strictly Lipschitzian single-valued mapping.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.3 Strictly Lipschitzian Behavior and Coderivative Scalarization p. 287
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(y^*\in\mathbb{R}^m\), define the scalarization \(\varphi_{y^*}(x):=\langle y^*,f(x)\rangle\). Under strict Lipschitzian behavior at \(\bar x\), the limiting coderivative admits the scalar representation
\[
D^*f(\bar x)(y^*)=\partial\varphi_{y^*}(\bar x)
=\partial\langle y^*,f\rangle(\bar x).
\]
Hence evaluating the dual mapping derivative at \(y^*\) reduces to computing the limiting subdifferential of a real-valued locally Lipschitz scalarization. The equality concerns limiting constructions on both sides; replacing either side by a regular or Clarke construction requires the corresponding variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly Lipschitzian mapping, applying the coderivative to a dual vector equals the limiting subdifferential of the mapping scalarized by that vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Coderivative Scalarization

children.title: Inverse-Graph Duality
children.top_down_role: Transformation of graphical derivatives and coderivatives under inversion.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graphical derivatives invert relationally, while coderivatives transform by coordinate exchange with the stated signs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inversion formulas under the standard limiting-coderivative sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because
\[
\operatorname{gph}F^{-1}=\{(y,x):(x,y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\},
\]
coordinate exchange yields, for \(v\in\mathbb{R}^m\),
\[
DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(v)=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:v\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\}.
\]
For the convention \(D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*):=\{x^*:(x^*,-y^*)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\}\), the corresponding dual formula is
\[
D^*F^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(x^*)
=\{y^*:-x^*\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(-y^*)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverting a set-valued mapping exchanges graph coordinates: graphical derivatives become inverse relations, and coderivatives obey the corresponding signed coordinate-exchange formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Graph Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate-exchange formulas appear consistent with the displayed coderivative convention, but the convention-sensitive signed dual formula has no authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Constraint-System Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Graphical encodings of implicit constraints and generalized equations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized equation \(0\in f(x)+Q(x)\) is the zero-level inverse image of the graphically represented mapping \(M=f+Q\).

notation.meaning: solution set of the generalized equation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph encoding of an unparameterized generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the constraint mapping \(M:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^m\) by \(M(x):=f(x)+Q(x)\). Its graph has the exact representation
\[
\operatorname{gph}M
=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m:z-f(x)\in Q(x)\}.
\]
The generalized equation and its solution set are therefore
\[
0\in f(x)+Q(x),\qquad
S:=\{x:0\in M(x)\}=M^{-1}(0)
=\{x:-f(x)\in Q(x)\}.
\]
Thus an implicit constraint system is encoded as membership of \((x,0)\) in a graph, permitting tangent, normal, derivative, and coderivative constructions to act on the same geometric object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized equation is represented by the graph of the sum mapping; feasible points are precisely the inverse image of zero under that mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-System Graph Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph and inverse-image identities are precise and mathematically standard, and representation is the correct content kind, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator as required by the evidence contract.

children.top_down_role: Exact convex subdifferential calculus under standard finite-dimensional or locally convex settings.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}g\), \(\partial(f+g)(x)=\partial f(x)+\partial g(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact convex subdifferential sum rule under relative-interior qualification.

source_refs.locator: 1.1.3 Calculus of Generalized Normals p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) and \(g\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). If
\[
\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\neq\varnothing,
\]
then for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}g\), the convex subdifferential sum rule is exact:
\[
\partial(f+g)(x)=\partial f(x)+\partial g(x).
\]
The right-hand side is the Minkowski sum of the two subdifferential sets. Without the qualification, the inclusion \(\partial f(x)+\partial g(x)\subseteq\partial(f+g)(x)\) remains valid, but equality need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For proper closed convex functions whose domains have intersecting relative interiors, the subdifferential of their sum equals the sum of their subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Calculus Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The relative-interior qualification for the finite convex family \(f_1,\ldots,f_p\) is
\[
\bigcap_{i=1}^p\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_i)\neq\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, there exists \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) lying in the relative interior of every effective domain. For two functions this becomes \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_1)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f_2)\neq\varnothing\). Under this condition, finite-dimensional convex sum calculus is exact; in particular, at each common-domain point \(x\),
\[
\partial\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^p f_i\Bigr)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p\partial f_i(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The qualification requires one point lying in the relative interior of every function’s effective domain; it supports exact finite-dimensional convex sum calculus.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete finite-dimensional failure of the convex normal-cone sum rule without relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge u^2\}\) and \(D=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\le -u^2\}\). Then \(C\cap D=\{(0,0)\}\) and \(\operatorname{ri}C\cap\operatorname{ri}D=\varnothing\). At \(z=(0,0)\), one has \(N_C(z)=\{(0,t):t\le0\}\), \(N_D(z)=\{(0,t):t\ge0\}\), and hence \(N_C(z)+N_D(z)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\), whereas \(N_{C\cap D}(z)=\mathbb R^2\). Thus the normal-cone intersection formula, equivalently the indicator-function subdifferential sum formula, can be strictly inexact when the convex interiority qualification is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two tangent convex regions meet only at the origin; their individual normals generate only a line, while the intersection normal is the entire plane.
assumptions_latex: \(C,D\subset\mathbb R^2\) are the displayed closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_C(0)+N_D(0)\subsetneq N_{C\cap D}(0).\]

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to C at z

knowledge_statements.title: Locally Lipschitz Clarke Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Clarke sum calculus for locally Lipschitz functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\). Their Clarke subdifferentials are nonempty compact convex sets, and the finite-sum rule is \[\partial_C\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(\bar x)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial_C f_i(\bar x).\] The inclusion is generally not an equality. If every \(f_i\) is Clarke regular at \(\bar x\), then directional derivatives add and the displayed inclusion becomes equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clarke calculus always gives a convexified subdifferential inclusion for finite sums of locally Lipschitz functions; regularity of all summands yields equality.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) for every \(i\).
Equality additionally assumes Clarke regularity of every summand at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial_C\!\left(\sum_i f_i\right)(\bar x)\subseteq\sum_i\partial_C f_i(\bar x),\quad\text{with equality under Clarke regularity}.\]

notation.meaning: Clarke subdifferential of f at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Clarke chain rules under regularity or smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three alternative sufficient regimes turn the locally Lipschitz chain-rule inclusion into equality; the first also preserves subdifferential regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f=g\circ h, where h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m is locally Lipschitz at x and g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R} is locally Lipschitz at h(x). (i) If g is subdifferentially regular at h(x), every h_i is subdifferentially regular at x, and every \alpha\in\partial_C g(h(x)) satisfies \alpha_i\geq0 for all i, then f is subdifferentially regular at x and \partial_C f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{H^T\alpha:H\in\partial_C h(x),\ \alpha\in\partial_C g(h(x))\}. (ii) If g is subdifferentially regular at h(x) and every h_i is continuously differentiable at x, then \partial_C f(x)=\nabla h(x)^T\partial_C g(h(x)). (iii) If m=1 and g is continuously differentiable at h(x), then \partial_C f(x)=g'(h(x))\partial_C h(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz composition, the Clarke chain rule is exact under three alternative regimes: regular outer and component functions with nonnegative outer subgradients; a regular outer function with a smooth inner map; or a scalar smooth outer function. The first regime also makes the composition subdifferentially regular.
assumptions_latex: \text{(i) }g\text{ and every }h_i\text{ are subdifferentially regular, and }\alpha_i\geq0\ \forall\alpha\in\partial_C g(h(x)),\ \forall i
\text{(ii) }g\text{ is subdifferentially regular and every }h_i\text{ is continuously differentiable at }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{(i) }f\text{ is subdifferentially regular and }\partial_C f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{H^T\alpha:H\in\partial_C h(x),\alpha\in\partial_C g(h(x))\};\\&\text{(ii) }\partial_C f(x)=\nabla h(x)^T\partial_C g(h(x));\\&\text{(iii) }\partial_C f(x)=g'(h(x))\partial_C h(x).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke subdifferential of a smooth outer composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here the adjoint Clarke derivative fan acts on the gradient of the scalar outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $y=F(x)$, let $f$ be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of $y$, and define $\varphi(x')=f(F(x'))$ for $x'\in X=\operatorname{dom}F$. Then $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz and
\[
\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}\varphi(x)=a_{\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}^{*}F(x)}\bigl(\nabla f(y)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the scalar outer function f is continuously differentiable near F(x), then the composition φ=f∘F is locally Lipschitz and its Clarke subdifferential at x is the action of the adjoint Clarke derivative fan of F at x on ∇f(F(x)).
assumptions_latex: f\in C^1\text{ on a neighborhood of }y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is locally Lipschitz and }\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}\varphi(x)=a_{\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}^{*}F(x)}\bigl(\nabla f(y)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epi-Lipschitzian Set Near a Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local coordinate definition for an arbitrary subset of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x\in C\). The set \(C\) is epi-Lipschitzian near \(x\) if there exist an invertible linear map \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times\mathbb{R}\), a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\), and a function \(\phi:\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}\), Lipschitz near the \(\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\)-component \(\xi\) of \(A(x)\), such that \[C\cap U=U\cap A^{-1}(\operatorname{epi}\phi).\] In these coordinates, the portion of \(\partial C\) in \(U\) is represented by the graph of \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is epi-Lipschitzian near one of its points when an invertible linear change of coordinates makes it locally the epigraph of a function that is Lipschitz near the transformed point. Its local boundary is then the graph of that function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists A,U,\phi:\quad C\cap U=U\cap A^{-1}(\operatorname{epi}\phi),\quad \phi\text{ is Lipschitz near }\xi=\pi_{\mathbb{R}^{n-1}}(A(x))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke chain-rule inclusion for a Lipschitz composite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composition rule with a vector-valued locally Lipschitz inner mapping and scalar locally Lipschitz outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be Lipschitz near \(x\), let \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz near \(F(x)\), and set \(\varphi=g\circ F\). Then \(\varphi\) is Lipschitz near \(x\) and
\[
\partial\varphi(x)\subset\operatorname{conv}\{Z^{\mathsf T}\xi:Z\in\partial F(x),\ \xi\in\partial g(F(x))\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite of locally Lipschitz mappings is locally Lipschitz, and its Clarke generalized gradient is contained in the convex hull of transposed generalized-Jacobian actions on generalized gradients of the outer function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is Lipschitz near }x\quad\text{and}\quad\partial\varphi(x)\subset\operatorname{conv}\{Z^{\mathsf T}\xi:Z\in\partial F(x),\ \xi\in\partial g(F(x))\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Regularity of a Locally Lipschitz Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise definition for a real-valued locally Lipschitz function on an open Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz on the open set \(\mathcal O\), and let \(\bar x\in\mathcal O\). Then \(\phi\) is Clarke regular (subdifferentially regular) at \(\bar x\) if it is directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\) and \(\widehat\partial\phi(\bar x)=\partial_C\phi(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz function is Clarke regular at a point when it is directionally differentiable there and its regular and Clarke subdifferentials coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi\text{ is Clarke regular at }\bar x\iff \phi\text{ is directionally differentiable at }\bar x\text{ and }\widehat\partial\phi(\bar x)=\partial_C\phi(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global, Local, and Relative Lipschitz Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a mapping between two metric spaces and an arbitrary subset of its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal X_1,d_1)\) and \((\mathcal X_2,d_2)\) be metric spaces, let \(T:\mathcal X_1\to\mathcal X_2\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathcal X_1\). For \(\beta\geq0\), \(T\) is Lipschitz continuous with constant \(\beta\) if \[\forall x,y\in\mathcal X_1,\qquad d_2(Tx,Ty)\leq\beta d_1(x,y).\] It is locally Lipschitz continuous near \(x\in\mathcal X_1\) if there exists \(\rho>0\) such that \(T|_{B(x;\rho)}\) is Lipschitz continuous, and it is locally Lipschitz continuous on \(C\) if this holds near every \(x\in C\). Finally, \(T\) is Lipschitz continuous relative to \(C\) with constant \(\beta\geq0\) if \[\forall x,y\in C,\qquad d_2(Tx,Ty)\leq\beta d_1(x,y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping between metric spaces is beta-Lipschitz when distances between all image pairs are at most beta times the corresponding domain distances. It is locally Lipschitz near a point when its restriction to some positive-radius ball about that point is Lipschitz, locally Lipschitz on a set when this holds at every point of the set, and beta-Lipschitz relative to a set when the distance inequality is required only for pairs in that set.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X_1,d_1)\) and \((\mathcal X_2,d_2)\) are metric spaces.
For statements involving a Lipschitz constant, \(\beta\in\mathbb R_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is globally, locally, locally on }C,\text{ or relatively to }C\text{ Lipschitz exactly under the corresponding quantified conditions above.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke chain-rule inclusion for a Lipschitz composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General locally Lipschitz composition rule; the conclusion is an inclusion rather than equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be Lipschitz near $x$, let $f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R$ be Lipschitz near $y=H(x)$, and set $\varphi=f\circ H$. Then
\[\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}\varphi(x)\subseteq\operatorname{co}\{A^*\ell':A\in\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}H(x),\ \ell'\in\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}f(y)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a composition of locally Lipschitz mappings, every Clarke subgradient of the composition lies in the convex hull of adjoint generalized-Jacobian images of Clarke subgradients of the outer function.
assumptions_latex: H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is Lipschitz near }x
f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\text{ is Lipschitz near }y=H(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}\varphi(x)\subseteq\operatorname{co}\{A^*\ell':A\in\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}H(x),\ \ell'\in\partial_{\mathrm{Cl}}f(H(x))\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local and Global Lipschitz Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines Lipschitz regularity at a point, on a set, and globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is locally Lipschitz at $x$ if there exist $K>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$ such that $|f(y)-f(z)|\le K\|y-z\|$ for all $y,z\in B(x;\varepsilon)$. It is locally Lipschitz on $U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ if this holds at every $x\in U$. It is Lipschitz on $U$ if there exists one constant $K$ such that $|f(y)-f(z)|\le K\|y-z\|$ for all $y,z\in U$. Taking $U=\mathbb{R}^n$ gives the corresponding global notions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is locally Lipschitz at a point when one Lipschitz bound holds throughout some neighborhood of that point. It is locally Lipschitz on a set when this holds at every point of the set, and Lipschitz on a set when a single constant controls every pair of points in the set. Setting the domain to all of Euclidean space gives the global notions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated inequalities define pointwise local, setwise local, and setwise/global Lipschitz continuity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Clarke directional growth on a segment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A locally Lipschitz segment mean-value lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be locally Lipschitz continuous on [\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}], and suppose f(\mathbf{x})<f(\mathbf{y}). Then there exists \mathbf{z}\in(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) such that f(\mathbf{z})>f(\mathbf{x}) and f^{\circ}(\mathbf{z};\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If f is locally Lipschitz on the segment from x to y and f(x) is less than f(y), some interior point z has value above f(x) and positive generalized directional growth toward y.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous on }[\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mathbf{z}\in(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}):\ f(\mathbf{z})>f(\mathbf{x})\land f^{\circ}(\mathbf{z};\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x})>0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz regularity of the directional-derivative map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical directional derivative at a differentiability point in the locally Lipschitz regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Suppose $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is differentiable at $x$ and is Lipschitz with constant $K$ on a neighborhood of $x$. Then $d\mapsto f'(x;d)$ is positively homogeneous and $K$-Lipschitz: for all $d,d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\lambda\geq0$, $f'(x;\lambda d)=\lambda f'(x;d)$ and $|f'(x;d_1)-f'(x;d_2)|\leq K\|d_1-d_2\|$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a differentiability point of a locally Lipschitz function, the directional derivative is positively homogeneous and Lipschitz in its direction argument with the same Lipschitz constant.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz with constant }K\text{ on a neighborhood of }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall d,d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \forall\lambda\geq0:\quad f'(x;\lambda d)=\lambda f'(x;d),\qquad |f'(x;d_1)-f'(x;d_2)|\leq K\|d_1-d_2\|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz and locally Lipschitz functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definitions of global and neighborhood Lipschitz regularity for real-valued functions on subsets of a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be a Banach space, let $Y\subseteq X$, and let $f:Y\to\mathbb R$. The function $f$ is Lipschitz on $Y$ if there exists $K\geq0$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\leq K\|u-v\|$ for all $u,v\in Y$. Define $B_X(x,\epsilon):=\{y\in X:\|x-y\|\leq\epsilon\}$. For $x\in Y$, the function is Lipschitz near $x$ if there exists $\epsilon>0$ with $B_X(x,\epsilon)\subseteq Y$ such that $f$ is Lipschitz on $B_X(x,\epsilon)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is Lipschitz on its domain when one constant bounds every change in value by the corresponding change in argument. It is Lipschitz near a point when this condition holds on a sufficiently small ball contained in its domain.
assumptions_latex: x\in Y\text{ for the local definition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz on }Y\iff\exists K\geq0\ \forall u,v\in Y:\ |f(u)-f(v)|\leq K\|u-v\|;\quad f\text{ is Lipschitz near }x\iff\exists\epsilon>0:\ B_X(x,\epsilon)\subseteq Y\text{ and }f|_{B_X(x,\epsilon)}\text{ is Lipschitz}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz norm bound for the discrete gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent uniform norm bound over all stated construction parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ be locally Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant }L>0.\text{ Then, for every }\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n,\ \mathbf g\in S_1,\ \mathbf e\in G,\ \lambda>0,\ z\in P,\text{ and }\alpha>0,\quad \|\Gamma^i\|\le C(n)L,\qquad C(n)=\bigl(n^2+2n^{3/2}-2n^{1/2}\bigr)^{1/2}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Subdifferential Quotient Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient calculus for locally Lipschitz functions with a nonzero denominator, including the nonnegative-positive subdifferentially regular equality case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be locally Lipschitz continuous at x\in\mathbb{R}^n, with f_2(x)\neq0. Then f_1/f_2 is locally Lipschitz continuous at x and
\[
\partial\!\left(\frac{f_1}{f_2}\right)(x)\subseteq\frac{f_2(x)\partial f_1(x)-f_1(x)\partial f_2(x)}{f_2(x)^2}.
\]
If, in addition, f_1(x)\geq0, f_2(x)>0, and f_1,f_2 are subdifferentially regular at x, then f_1/f_2 is subdifferentially regular at x and equality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two functions are locally Lipschitz at x and the denominator is nonzero there, their quotient is locally Lipschitz and satisfies the stated subdifferential inclusion. If the numerator value is nonnegative, the denominator value is positive, and both functions are subdifferentially regular at x, the quotient is regular and equality holds.
assumptions_latex: f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ are locally Lipschitz continuous at }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{f_1}{f_2}\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous at }x\text{ and }\partial\!\left(\frac{f_1}{f_2}\right)(x)\subseteq\frac{f_2(x)\partial f_1(x)-f_1(x)\partial f_2(x)}{f_2(x)^2};\text{ if }f_1(x)\geq0,f_2(x)>0\text{ and both functions are subdifferentially regular at }x,\text{ then the quotient is subdifferentially regular and equality holds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Subdifferential Sum Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sum calculus for locally Lipschitz functions, including equality when one summand is continuously differentiable near the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Generalized Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual definition by domination of linear directional forms by the Clarke generalized directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz near \(x\). The Clarke generalized gradient of \(f\) at \(x\) is
\[
\partial f(x):=\left\{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid \langle\xi,h\rangle\le f^0(x;h)\text{ for every }h\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}.
\]
Its elements are called generalized subgradients of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function Lipschitz near x, the Clarke generalized gradient consists of the vectors whose inner product with every direction is bounded above by the Clarke generalized directional derivative in that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f(x)=\left\{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid \langle\xi,h\rangle\le f^0(x;h)\ \forall h\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Characterization and Bounds for Epsilon-Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence with the epigraphical Lipschitz-like property and uniform local norm estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be finite around \(\bar x\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Then \(\varphi\) is Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\) if and only if its epigraphical multifunction \(E_\varphi\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\varphi(\bar x))\). If \(\varphi\) is Lipschitz around \(\bar x\) with modulus \(\ell\ge0\), there exists \(\eta>0\) such that, for every \(x\in\bar x+\eta\mathbb B\), \(\|x^*\|\le\varepsilon(1+\ell)\) whenever \((x^*,0)\in\widehat N_\varepsilon((x,\varphi(x));\operatorname{epi}\varphi)\), \(\|x^*\|\le\ell+\varepsilon(1+\ell)\) whenever \(x^*\in\widehat\partial_{g\varepsilon}\varphi(x)\), and \(\|x^*\|\le\ell+\varepsilon\) whenever \(x^*\in\widehat\partial_{a\varepsilon}\varphi(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function finite near the reference point is locally Lipschitz exactly when its epigraphical multifunction is locally Lipschitz-like. With Lipschitz modulus ell, all nearby horizontal epsilon-normals, geometric epsilon-subgradients, and analytic epsilon-subgradients satisfy the stated uniform norm bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\text{ is Lipschitz around }\bar x\text{ with modulus }\ell\ge0\) for the norm estimates
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\text{ is locally Lipschitz at }\bar x\iff E_\varphi\text{ is Lipschitz-like at }(\bar x,\varphi(\bar x))\), with the three stated local norm bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke generalized-gradient characterization and finite-sum inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The finite-sum calculus rule is an inclusion; equality is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X$ be a normed space and let $f$ be Lipschitz on a neighborhood of $x$. For $\xi\in X^*$,
\[
\xi\in\partial f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f^o(x;d)\geq\langle\xi,d\rangle\quad\forall d\in X.
\]
If $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ are Lipschitz on a neighborhood of $x$, then $\sum_{i=1}^m f_i$ is Lipschitz there and
\[
\partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x),
\]
where the right-hand side is a Minkowski sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual functional belongs to the Clarke generalized gradient exactly when its pairing with every direction is bounded above by the Clarke generalized directional derivative. A finite sum of locally Lipschitz functions is locally Lipschitz, and its Clarke generalized gradient is contained in the Minkowski sum of the individual generalized gradients.
assumptions_latex: $f$ is Lipschitz on a neighborhood of $x$.
$m\in\mathbb N$ and each $f_i$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, is Lipschitz on a neighborhood of $x$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \xi\in\partial f(x)\iff\bigl(f^o(x;d)\geq\langle\xi,d\rangle\ \forall d\in X\bigr);\qquad \partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)\subseteq\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz and locally Lipschitz mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions on Euclidean spaces, including extended-real functions restricted to their finite domain and vector-valued maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $L\geq0$ and let $C\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f$. A function $f:\mathbf E\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ is Lipschitz on $C$ with constant $L$ if $|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in C$. It is locally Lipschitz around $z$ if this condition holds on some neighborhood of $z$. For $F:\mathbf E\to\mathbf Y$, where $\mathbf Y$ is Euclidean, replace the scalar absolute value by $\|F(x)-F(y)\|$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is Lipschitz with constant L on a subset of its domain when every pair of function values differs by at most L times the distance between the points. It is locally Lipschitz around a point when this holds on a neighborhood of that point. The analogous definition for Euclidean vector-valued maps uses the norm of the output difference.
assumptions_latex: $f:\mathbf E\to(-\infty,+\infty]$; analogously $F:\mathbf E\to\mathbf Y$ for Euclidean $\mathbf Y$
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: $|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|\quad\forall x,y\in C$, with $\|F(x)-F(y)\|$ in the vector-valued case.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Membership characterization and semicontinuity of the Clarke generalized gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The neighborhood identity holds in the extracted form; finite dimensionality is required only for the stated upper-semicontinuity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f$ be Lipschitz near $x$. Then, for $\xi\in X^*$,
\[
\xi\in\partial f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f^o(x;d)\ge\langle\xi,d\rangle\quad\forall d\in X.
\]
Moreover, with $B(0,\delta)=\{z\in X:\|z\|\le\delta\}$,
\[
\partial f(x)=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\ \bigcup_{y\in x+B(0,\delta)}\partial f(y).
\]
If $X$ is finite-dimensional, the multifunction $x\mapsto\partial f(x)$ is upper semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual vector belongs to the Clarke generalized gradient at x exactly when its pairing with every direction is bounded above by the Clarke generalized directional derivative. The generalized gradient also equals the intersection, over all neighborhood radii, of the unions of nearby generalized gradients. In finite dimensions the generalized-gradient mapping is upper semicontinuous.
assumptions_latex: $f$ is Lipschitz on a neighborhood of $x$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \xi\in\partial f(x)\iff \bigl(f^o(x;d)\ge\langle\xi,d\rangle\ \forall d\in X\bigr),\quad \partial f(x)=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\bigcup_{y\in x+B(0,\delta)}\partial f(y);\quad \dim X<\infty\Rightarrow \partial f\text{ is upper semicontinuous}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Subdifferential Product Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product calculus for two locally Lipschitz functions, including the nonnegative subdifferentially regular equality case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be locally Lipschitz continuous at x\in\mathbb{R}^n. Then f_1f_2 is locally Lipschitz continuous at x and
\[
\partial(f_1f_2)(x)\subseteq f_2(x)\partial f_1(x)+f_1(x)\partial f_2(x).
\]
If, in addition, f_1(x),f_2(x)\geq 0 and f_1,f_2 are subdifferentially regular at x, then f_1f_2 is subdifferentially regular at x and equality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The product of two functions locally Lipschitz at x is locally Lipschitz there and satisfies the stated subdifferential inclusion. When both values are nonnegative and both functions are subdifferentially regular at x, the product is regular and the inclusion becomes equality.
assumptions_latex: f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ are locally Lipschitz continuous at }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_1f_2\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous at }x\text{ and }\partial(f_1f_2)(x)\subseteq f_2(x)\partial f_1(x)+f_1(x)\partial f_2(x);\text{ if }f_1(x),f_2(x)\geq0\text{ and both functions are subdifferentially regular at }x,\text{ then }f_1f_2\text{ is subdifferentially regular and equality holds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Goldstein ε-Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for a locally Lipschitz real-valued function at a specified point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) locally Lipschitz at \(x\) and \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), the Goldstein \(\varepsilon\)-subdifferential is
\[\partial_\varepsilon^G f(x):=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{y\in B(x;\varepsilon)}\partial f(y)\right).\]
Every \(\xi\in\partial_\varepsilon^G f(x)\) is called a Goldstein \(\varepsilon\)-subgradient of \(f\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Goldstein epsilon-subdifferential is the closed convex hull of all subdifferentials at points in the epsilon-ball about x; its elements are epsilon-subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_\varepsilon^G f(x)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{y\in B(x;\varepsilon)}\partial f(y)\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke chain rule for a scalar outer function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for a locally Lipschitz scalar function and a locally Lipschitz vector map, including equality regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m be locally Lipschitz at x, let g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R be locally Lipschitz at G(x), and set f=g\circ G. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Baseline semismooth complementarity-operator assumptions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke mean-value inclusion for Lipschitz mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional mean-value theorem for a vector-valued locally Lipschitz mapping and its Clarke generalized Jacobians along a segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, let \(F:U\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be Lipschitz on \(U\), and let \(x,y\in U\). Then
\[
F(y)-F(x)\in\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\partial F([x,y])(y-x)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
\partial F([x,y])(y-x):=\{Z(y-x):z\in[x,y],\ Z\in\partial F(z)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a vector-valued mapping that is Lipschitz on an open convex set, the increment between two points lies in the convex hull of generalized-Jacobian actions evaluated along their connecting segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(y)-F(x)\in\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\partial F([x,y])(y-x)\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness and support representation of the Clarke generalized gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic properties at a point where the function is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X$ be a normed space and let $f:X\to\mathbb R$ be Lipschitz with constant $K$ on a neighborhood of $x$. Then $\partial f(x)$ is a nonempty, convex, weak-$*$ compact subset of $X^*$, every $\xi\in\partial f(x)$ satisfies $\|\xi\|_*\le K$, and, for every $d\in X$,
\[
f^o(x;d)=\max_{\xi\in\partial f(x)}\langle\xi,d\rangle.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If f is Lipschitz with constant K near x, its Clarke generalized gradient at x is nonempty, convex, weak-star compact, and contained in the dual ball of radius K. The Clarke generalized directional derivative in every direction is the maximum pairing with an element of that generalized gradient.
assumptions_latex: $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is Lipschitz with constant $K$ on a neighborhood of $x$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f(x)\subset X^*\text{ is nonempty, convex, and weak-$*$ compact},\quad \|\xi\|_*\le K\ (\forall\xi\in\partial f(x)),\quad f^o(x;d)=\max_{\xi\in\partial f(x)}\langle\xi,d\rangle\ (\forall d\in X).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-Limit Representation of the Goldstein ε-Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation by limiting gradients at differentiability points converging to points in the ε-ball.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz, Lipschitz Near a Point, and Locally Lipschitz Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a single-valued mapping between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(F:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(\lambda\ge 0\). The mapping \(F\) is Lipschitz on \(\Omega\) with modulus \(\lambda\) if \(\|F(x_1)-F(x_2)\|\le \lambda\|x_1-x_2\|\) for all \(x_1,x_2\in\Omega\). It is Lipschitz near \(x\) with modulus \(\lambda\) if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that it is Lipschitz with that modulus on \(x+\varepsilon\mathbb{B}\) (within its domain). It is locally Lipschitz on \(\Omega\) if it is Lipschitz near every \(x\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is Lipschitz with modulus lambda when output distances are at most lambda times input distances. It is Lipschitz near a point when this holds on some neighborhood of that point, and locally Lipschitz when it holds near every point of its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|F(x_1)-F(x_2)\|\le\lambda\|x_1-x_2\|\quad\forall x_1,x_2\in\Omega,\quad\text{with the stated neighborhood and pointwise variants.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Properties of the Goldstein ε-Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-radius consistency, radius monotonicity, compactness and boundedness, and upper semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz at \(x\) with Lipschitz constant \(K\). Then
\[(i)\quad \partial_0^Gf(x)=\partial f(x),\]
\[(ii)\quad \varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\implies \partial_{\varepsilon_1}^Gf(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon_2}^Gf(x),\]
\[(iii)\quad \partial_\varepsilon^Gf(x)\text{ is nonempty, convex, and compact, and }\partial_\varepsilon^Gf(x)\subseteq B(0;K),\]
and the set-valued mapping \(x\mapsto\partial_\varepsilon^Gf(x)\) is upper semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At radius zero the Goldstein subdifferential equals the ordinary locally Lipschitz subdifferential. It grows monotonically with the radius, is nonempty, convex, compact, and bounded by the Lipschitz constant, and its set-valued mapping is upper semicontinuous.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is locally Lipschitz at }x\in\mathbb{R}^n\text{ with Lipschitz constant }K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_0^Gf(x)=\partial f(x),\quad \varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\Rightarrow\partial_{\varepsilon_1}^Gf(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon_2}^Gf(x),\quad \varnothing\ne\partial_\varepsilon^Gf(x)\subseteq B(0;K),\quad \partial_\varepsilon^Gf\text{ is upper semicontinuous}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Subdifferential Rule for a Finite Maximum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-index calculus for a finite maximum of locally Lipschitz functions, with equality under componentwise subdifferential regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be locally Lipschitz continuous at x for i=1,\ldots,m, and define
\[
f(y)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}f_i(y),\qquad I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:f_i(x)=f(x)\}.
\]
Then f is locally Lipschitz continuous at x and
\[
\partial f(x)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}\partial f_i(x)\right).
\]
If every f_i is subdifferentially regular at x, then f is subdifferentially regular at x and equality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite maximum of functions locally Lipschitz at x is locally Lipschitz there. Its subdifferential is contained in the convex hull of the subdifferentials of the active components. If every component is subdifferentially regular at x, the maximum is regular and equality holds.
assumptions_latex: f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous at }x\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is locally Lipschitz continuous at }x\text{ and }\partial f(x)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}\partial f_i(x)\right);\text{ if every }f_i\text{ is subdifferentially regular at }x,\text{ then }f\text{ is subdifferentially regular and equality holds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz condition and local Lipschitz continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a real-valued function on a subset of a normed space and on a neighborhood contained in its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subset X\), \(f:Y\to\mathbb R\), and \(K\ge0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Mean Value Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonsmooth mean-value theorem along a line segment contained in an open domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be open, let \(x^1,x^2\in X\), and suppose \([x^1,x^2]\subset X\). Define \(x_t=x^1+t(x^2-x^1)\). If \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz, then there exists \(\theta\in(0,1)\) such that
\[
f_{\mathrm{Cl}}^{\downarrow}(x_\theta,x^2-x^1)\le f(x^2)-f(x^1)\le f_{\mathrm{Cl}}^{\uparrow}(x_\theta,x^2-x^1).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any segment contained in the open domain of a locally Lipschitz function, some interior point of the segment has lower and upper Clarke directional derivatives in the segment direction that bound the function-value difference between the endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\theta\in(0,1):\quad f_{\mathrm{Cl}}^{\downarrow}(x_\theta,x^2-x^1)\le f(x^2)-f(x^1)\le f_{\mathrm{Cl}}^{\uparrow}(x_\theta,x^2-x^1)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise C^k Map and Essentially Active Pieces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines locally finite piecewise-C^k structure for vector-valued maps and its active-index notions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let V\subset\mathbb{R}^n be open and 1\le k\le\infty. A map f:V\to\mathbb{R}^m is PC^k if it is continuous and, for every x_0\in V, there are a neighborhood W\subset V of x_0 and finitely many C^k maps f^i:W\to\mathbb{R}^m, i=1,\ldots,N, such that f(x)\in\{f^1(x),\ldots,f^N(x)\} for every x\in W. For such a representation, I(x):=\{i:f(x)=f^i(x)\}, and I^e(x):=\{i\in I(x):x\in\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{int}\{y\in W:f(y)=f^i(y)\})\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PC^k map is a continuous finite-dimensional map that locally agrees at every point with one of finitely many C^k maps. Its active indices are the pieces agreeing at the point, and an active index is essentially active when the point lies in the closure of the interior of that piece's selection region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in PC^k\iff \forall x_0\in V\;\exists W,\,f^1,\ldots,f^N\in C^k(W;\mathbb{R}^m)\;\forall x\in W:\ f(x)\in\{f^1(x),\ldots,f^N(x)\},\quad I(x),I^e(x)\text{ as defined above}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry and Support Representation of the Clarke Generalized Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonemptiness, compact convex geometry, the support-function representation, and continuity properties under local Lipschitz regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be Lipschitz near \(x\) with modulus \(\lambda\). Then \(\partial f(x)\) is nonempty, convex, and compact, and
\[
\partial f(x)\subseteq\lambda\mathbb{B}.
\]
For every \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
f^0(x;h)=\max_{\xi\in\partial f(x)}\langle\xi,h\rangle.
\]
Moreover, the multifunction \(y\mapsto\partial f(y)\) is upper semicontinuous and closed at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function Lipschitz near x with modulus lambda, its Clarke generalized gradient at x is a nonempty compact convex subset of the radius-lambda ball. Its support function is the Clarke generalized directional derivative, and the generalized-gradient mapping is upper semicontinuous and closed at x.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz near }x\text{ with modulus }\lambda
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varnothing\ne\partial f(x)\subseteq\lambda\mathbb{B},\quad \partial f(x)\text{ is convex and compact},\quad f^0(x;h)=\max_{\xi\in\partial f(x)}\langle\xi,h\rangle\ \forall h,\quad \partial f(\cdot)\text{ is upper semicontinuous and closed at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise coderivative criteria for linear suboptimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient, necessary, and equivalent coderivative conditions for the mapping \(F\) associated with \((f,\Omega,\Theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the mapping associated with \((f,\Omega,\Theta)\). (i) If \(\dim X<\infty\) and some \(0
e z^*\in Z^*\) satisfies \(0\in D_M^*F( ar x,0)(z^*)\), then \( ar x\) is linearly suboptimal. (ii) Conversely, linear suboptimality implies the existence of \(0
e z^*\in Z^*\) with \(0\in\widetilde D_M^*F( ar x,0)(z^*)\), provided \(X,Z\) are Asplund, \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is locally closed at \(( ar x,0)\), and \(F^{-1}\) is PSNC at \((0, ar x)\); PSNC is automatic if \(\dim Z<\infty\) or \(F\) is metrically regular around \(( ar x,0)\). (iii) If \(\dim X<\infty\), \(Z\) is Asplund, \(F\) has locally closed graph and is SNC and strongly coderivatively normal at \(( ar x,0)\), with \(D^*F=D_M^*F=D_N^*F\) there, then linear suboptimality is equivalent to the existence of \(0

Under Asplund, closed-graph, and PSNC assumptions, linear suboptimality yields a nonzero multiplier satisfying the corresponding outer mixed-coderivative condition. Under finite-dimensional X, Asplund Z, SNC, strong coderivative normality, and equality of the relevant coderivatives, the pointwise coderivative condition is equivalent to linear suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relations among limiting and approximate normals and subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preserves the distinct assumptions and conclusions for approximate subgradients, G-normal constructions, and G-subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\varphi\) is lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\), then \(\partial\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial_A^\sigma\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial_A\varphi(\bar x)\). If \(\varphi\) is also Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\), then \(\operatorname{cl}^*\partial\varphi(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}^*\partial_A^\sigma\varphi(\bar x)=\partial_A\varphi(\bar x)\); if additionally \(X\) is WCG, then the three unclosed sets are equal. If \(\Omega\subset X\) is closed around \(\bar x\in\Omega\), then \(N(\bar x;\Omega)\subset\widetilde N_G^\sigma(\bar x;\Omega)\subset\widetilde N_G(\bar x;\Omega)\subset N_G(\bar x;\Omega)=\operatorname{cl}^*N(\bar x;\Omega)\); if \(X\) is WCG, then \(N(\bar x;\Omega)=\widetilde N_G^\sigma(\bar x;\Omega)=\widetilde N_G(\bar x;\Omega)\). If \(\varphi\) is lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\), then \(\partial\varphi(\bar x)\subset\widetilde\partial_G^\sigma\varphi(\bar x)\subset\widetilde\partial_G\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial_G\varphi(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}^*\partial\varphi(\bar x)\); if \(\varphi\) is also Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\) and \(X\) is WCG, all four sets are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting normals and subgradients lie inside the corresponding sequential approximate and approximate constructions. Local Lipschitz continuity yields weak-star closure identities, while the stated WCG hypotheses strengthen the indicated comparisons to exact equalities.
assumptions_latex: \text{For (i), }\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\text{ and }\varphi\text{ is lower semicontinuous around }\bar x
\text{For the closure refinement in (i), }\varphi\text{ is Lipschitz continuous around }\bar x
\text{For the exact equality in (i), }X\text{ is WCG}
\text{For the equality in (iii), }\varphi\text{ is Lipschitz continuous around }\bar x\text{ and }X\text{ is WCG}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial_A^\sigma\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial_A\varphi(\bar x);\quad N(\bar x;\Omega)\subset\widetilde N_G^\sigma(\bar x;\Omega)\subset\widetilde N_G(\bar x;\Omega)\subset N_G(\bar x;\Omega)=\operatorname{cl}^*N(\bar x;\Omega);\quad \partial\varphi(\bar x)\subset\widetilde\partial_G^\sigma\varphi(\bar x)\subset\widetilde\partial_G\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial_G\varphi(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}^*\partial\varphi(\bar x),\text{ with the stated Lipschitz and WCG refinements}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fréchet-subgradient characterization of constancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local and connected-domain constancy criteria for proper lower-semicontinuous functions on an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(U\subset X\) be open. Then \(\varphi\) is locally constant on \(U\) if and only if \[x^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(x)\Longrightarrow x^*=0\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\] If \(U\) is connected, this condition is equivalent to \(\varphi\) being constant on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open subset of an Asplund space, a proper lower-semicontinuous function is locally constant exactly when every Fréchet subgradient at every point is zero. If the open set is connected, this is equivalent to constancy on the whole set.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(U\) is additionally connected for the global-constancy equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\text{ is locally constant on }U\Longleftrightarrow\forall x\in U,\ \widehat\partial\varphi(x)\subset\{0\}\); if \(U\) is connected, these conditions are equivalent to \(\varphi\text{ being constant on }U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mean-value inequalities for lower-semicontinuous functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Fréchet-subgradient mean-value consequences for proper lower-semicontinuous functions on an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an Asplund space and let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, with \(\varphi(a)\in\mathbb R\). For every \(b\in X\), there exist \(c\in[a,b]\), \(x_k\to c\), and \(x_k^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(x_k)\) such that \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\langle x_k^*,b-a\rangle\ge\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)\). Moreover, for every \(b\in X\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), \[|\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)|\le\|b-a\|\sup\{\|x^*\|:x^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(c),\ c\in[a,b]+\varepsilon\mathbb B\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an Asplund space, a proper lower-semicontinuous function finite at the initial point satisfies a sequential Fréchet-subgradient mean-value inequality along every segment from that point. Its endpoint variation is bounded by the segment length times the supremum of nearby Fréchet-subgradient norms.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall b\in X\ \exists c\in[a,b],\ x_k\to c,\ x_k^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(x_k):\liminf_k\langle x_k^*,b-a\rangle\ge\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)\), and for every \(b\in X\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), \(|\varphi(b)-\varphi(a)|\le\|b-a\|\sup\{\|x^*\|:x^*\in\widehat\partial\varphi(c),\ c\in[a,b]+\varepsilon\mathbb B\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting representations of singular subgradients in Asplund spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential outer-limit representations using Fréchet and approximate Fréchet subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, and let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\). Then
\[
\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x)=\mathop{\operatorname{Limsup}}_{\substack{x\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x\\ \lambda\downarrow0}}\lambda\widehat\partial\varphi(x)=\mathop{\operatorname{Limsup}}_{\substack{x\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x\\ \varepsilon,\lambda\downarrow0}}\lambda\widehat\partial_\varepsilon\varphi(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper function lower semicontinuous near a domain point in an Asplund space, the singular subdifferential is the sequential outer limit of vanishing positive multiples of either Fréchet subgradients or approximate Fréchet subgradients along function-value convergence to the reference point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential characterization of sequential normal epi-compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An if-and-only-if characterization of SNEC through weak-star-to-norm convergence of scaled Fréchet subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, and let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\). Then \(\varphi\) is SNEC at \(\bar x\) if and only if, for every choice of sequences
\[
x_k\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x,\qquad \lambda_k\downarrow0,\qquad x_k^*\in\lambda_k\widehat\partial\varphi(x_k),
\]
one has
\[
x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lVert x_k^*\rVert\to0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper function lower semicontinuous near a domain point in an Asplund space is sequentially normally epi-compact there if and only if every weak-star-null sequence of scaled Fréchet subgradients, formed along function-value convergence with positive scales decreasing to zero, converges to zero in norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is SNEC at }\bar x\iff\left[\forall\,x_k\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x,\ \lambda_k\downarrow0,\ x_k^*\in\lambda_k\widehat\partial\varphi(x_k),\quad x_k^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\Rightarrow\lVert x_k^*\rVert\to0\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: PSNC and strong PSNC in product spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise compactness conditions for approximate regular normals in finite products of Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\prod_{j=1}^mX_j\), \(\bar x\in\Omega\), and \(J\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The set \(\Omega\) is PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(J\) if, for every \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), \(x_k\xrightarrow{\Omega}\bar x\), and \(x_k^*=(x_{1k}^*,\ldots,x_{mk}^*)\in\widehat N_{\varepsilon_k}(x_k;\Omega)\), the conditions \(x_{jk}^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\) for \(j\in J\) and \(\|x_{jk}^*\|\to0\) for \(j\notin J\) imply \(\|x_{jk}^*\|\to0\) for every \(j\in J\). It is strongly PSNC with respect to \(J\) if weak-star convergence \(x_{jk}^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\) for all \(j\) implies norm convergence for every \(j\in J\). For \(J=\varnothing\) both properties are automatic; for \(J=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) both reduce to SNC. For \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\), PSNC of \(F\) is PSNC of \(\operatorname{gph}F\) with respect to \(X\). If every \(X_j\) is Asplund and \(\Omega\) is locally closed around \(\bar x\), one may equivalently use \(\varepsilon_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSNC converts weak-star vanishing into norm vanishing on selected coordinates when all unselected normal components already vanish in norm. Strong PSNC requires only weak-star vanishing of every component. The empty-coordinate case is automatic, the full-coordinate case is ordinary SNC, and graph PSNC recovers the corresponding mapping property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{PSNC}_J:\ [x_{jk}^*\overset{w^*}{\to}0\ (j\in J),\ \|x_{jk}^*\|\to0\ (j\notin J)]\Rightarrow\|x_{jk}^*\|\to0\ (j\in J)\), with strong PSNC obtained by assuming weak-star convergence for all components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic-normal intersection rule in product Asplund spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone intersection calculus under complementary coordinate compactness and limiting qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(X_j\) be Asplund and let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset\prod_{j=1}^mX_j\) be locally closed around \(\bar x\in\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\). Let \(J_1,J_2\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfy \(J_1\cup J_2=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). If \(\Omega_1\) is PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(J_1\), \(\Omega_2\) is strongly PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(J_2\), and \(\{\Omega_1,\Omega_2\}\) satisfies the limiting qualification condition at \(\bar x\), then \(N(\bar x;\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)\subset N(\bar x;\Omega_1)+N(\bar x;\Omega_2)\). If both sets are normally regular at \(\bar x\), then their intersection is normally regular there and the inclusion is an equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementary PSNC and strong-PSNC assumptions, together with limiting qualification, yield the limiting-normal intersection inclusion. Normal regularity of both sets gives equality and normal regularity of the intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega_1\) is PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(J_1\)
\(\Omega_2\) is strongly PSNC at \(\bar x\) with respect to \(J_2\)
The limiting qualification condition holds at \(\bar x\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(\bar x;\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)\subset N(\bar x;\Omega_1)+N(\bar x;\Omega_2)\); if both sets are normally regular at \(\bar x\), equality holds and \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\) is normally regular at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner-Product Rule for Coderivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal and mixed coderivative estimate for the scalar multifunction obtained by pairing values of two multifunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\alpha\in\langle F_1,F_2\rangle(\bar x)\), choose \(\bar y_i\in F_i(\bar x)\) with \(\bar\alpha=\langle\bar y_1,\bar y_2\rangle\), and suppose that \(\operatorname{gph}F_i\) is locally closed around \((\bar x,\bar y_i)\), \(i=1,2\). Suppose also that \[(x,\alpha)\mapsto\{(y_1,y_2)\in Y^2:y_i\in F_i(x),\ \alpha=\langle y_1,y_2\rangle\}\] is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x,\bar\alpha,\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\), that at least one of \(F_1,F_2\) is PSNC at its reference point, and that qualification condition (3.19) holds. Then, for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) and for either coderivative variant \(D^*\in\{D_N^*,D_M^*\}\) inherited from Theorem 3.18, \[D^*\langle F_1,F_2\rangle(\bar x,\bar\alpha)(\lambda)\subset D_M^*F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(\lambda\bar y_2)+D_M^*F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)(\lambda\bar y_1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated inner-semicontinuity, local graph-closedness, PSNC, and qualification assumptions, each applicable coderivative of the scalar inner-product multifunction is contained in the sum of the mixed coderivatives of the two factors evaluated at the correspondingly scaled opposite reference values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic normal-cone estimate for inverse images
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-normal inverse-image rule under inner semicompactness and pointwise SNC/PSNC and mixed-coderivative qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) have closed graph, let \(\Theta\subset Y\) be closed, and let \(\bar x\in F^{-1}(\Theta)\). Suppose \(x\mapsto F(x)\cap\Theta\) is inner semicompact at \(\bar x\). Then
\[
N\bigl(\bar x;F^{-1}(\Theta)\bigr)\subset\bigcup_{\bar y\in F(\bar x)\cap\Theta}\bigcup_{y^*\in N(\bar y;\Theta)}D_N^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*).
\]

x\mapsto F(x)\cap\Theta\text{ is inner semicompact at }\bar x
\forall\bar y\in F(\bar x)\cap\Theta:\quad F^{-1}\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar y,\bar x)\ \text{or}\ \Theta\text{ is SNC at }\bar y
\forall\bar y\in F(\bar x)\cap\Theta:\quad N(\bar y;\Theta)\cap\ker\widetilde D_M^*F(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Horizontal normals to graphs of continuous functions in Asplund spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential realization of horizontal Fréchet normals and identification of the coderivative at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, and let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be finite and continuous around \(\bar x\in X\). Then:

(i) If
\[
(x^*,0)\in\widehat N\big((\bar x,\varphi(\bar x));\operatorname{gph}\varphi\big),
\]
then there exist sequences \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(\lambda_k\downarrow0\), and \(x_k^*\to x^*\) such that
\[
x_k^*\in\widehat\partial(\lambda_k\varphi)(x_k)\cup\widehat\partial(-\lambda_k\varphi)(x_k)\qquad(k\in\mathbb N).
\]

(ii)
\[
D^*\varphi(\bar x)(0)=\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x)\cup\partial^\infty(-\varphi)(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function finite and continuous near a point in an Asplund space, each horizontal Fréchet normal to its graph is a norm limit of Fréchet subgradients of vanishing positive or negative scalings of the function. The coderivative at zero is the union of the singular subdifferentials of the function and its negative.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is finite and continuous around }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[(x^*,0)\in\widehat N((\bar x,\varphi(\bar x));\operatorname{gph}\varphi)\Rightarrow\exists\,x_k\to\bar x,\ \lambda_k\downarrow0,\ x_k^*\to x^*:\ \forall k\in\mathbb N,\ x_k^*\in\widehat\partial(\lambda_k\varphi)(x_k)\cup\widehat\partial(-\lambda_k\varphi)(x_k)\right]\land\left[D^*\varphi(\bar x)(0)=\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x)\cup\partial^\infty(-\varphi)(\bar x)\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative single-valuedness and strict weak Hadamard differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives forward and converse links between strict weak differentiability and mixed or normal coderivative single-valuedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to Y\), where \(X\) is Asplund and \(Y\) is Banach. If \(f\) is strictly \(w\mathcal H\)-differentiable at \(\bar x\), then \(D_M^*f(\bar x)\) is a single-valued bounded linear operator satisfying \(D_M^*f(\bar x)(y^*)=\{\nabla\langle y^*,f\rangle(\bar x)\}\) for every \(y^*\in Y^*\). If the sequential convergence condition of Definition 3.25(ii) also holds, the same conclusion holds for \(D_N^*f(\bar x)\). Conversely, if \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\) and either \(D_M^*f(\bar x)\) or \(D_N^*f(\bar x)\) is single-valued, then \(f\) is strictly \(w\mathcal H\)-differentiable at \(\bar x\), with the corresponding formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict weak Hadamard differentiability makes the mixed coderivative a single-valued bounded linear operator given by the strict Hadamard derivatives of the dual scalarizations. The normal coderivative has the same property under the stated sequential condition. Conversely, local Lipschitz continuity and single-valuedness of either coderivative imply strict weak Hadamard differentiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{strict}\ w\mathcal H\text{-differentiability}\Rightarrow D_M^*f(\bar x)(y^*)=\{\nabla\langle y^*,f\rangle(\bar x)\};\quad \text{under the sequential condition, likewise for }D_N^*;\quad \text{local Lipschitzness and single-valued }D_M^*\text{ or }D_N^*\Rightarrow\operatorname{strict}\ w\mathcal H\text{-differentiability}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative Rules for h-Compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal and mixed coderivative estimates for locally Lipschitz or strictly differentiable coupling mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_i:X\rightrightarrows Y_i\), \(i=1,2\), let \(h:Y_1\times Y_2\to Z\), and let \(\bar z\in(F_1\diamond^hF_2)(\bar x)\). Define \[S(x,z)=\{(y_1,y_2)\in Y_1\times Y_2:y_i\in F_i(x),\ z=h(y_1,y_2)\}.\] Suppose that \(S\) is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}S\), each \(\operatorname{gph}F_i\) is locally closed around \((\bar x,\bar y_i)\), at least one of \(F_1,F_2\) is PSNC at its reference point, and qualification condition (3.19) holds. For every \(z^*\in Z^*\): (i) if \(h\) is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar y\), then, for the normal or mixed coderivative, \[D^*(F_1\diamond^hF_2)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)\subset\bigcup_{y^*\in D^*h(\bar y)(z^*)}\left[D_N^*F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(y_1^*)+D_N^*F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)(y_2^*)\right].\] (ii) If \(h\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar y\), then \[D_M^*(F_1\diamond^hF_2)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)\subset D_M^*F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(\nabla_1h(\bar y)^*z^*)+D_M^*F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)(\nabla_2h(\bar y)^*z^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under inner semicontinuity, local graph closedness, PSNC of at least one component, and qualification condition (3.19), the coderivative of an h-composition is bounded by sums of component coderivatives. A locally Lipschitz coupling gives a union over its coderivative values, while a strictly differentiable coupling gives adjoint partial-derivative pullbacks.
assumptions_latex: \bar z\in(F_1\diamond^hF_2)(\bar x),\quad \bar y=(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar z)
S\text{ is inner semicontinuous at }(\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)
\operatorname{gph}F_i\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y_i),\quad i=1,2
F_1\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y_1)\text{ or }F_2\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y_2)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed locally Lipschitz and strictly differentiable coderivative inclusions hold for every }z^*\in Z^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized-normal rules for Minkowski sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular and limiting normal estimates expressed through decompositions of a point in the sum of two closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be Asplund, let \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subset X\) be closed, let \(\bar x\in\Omega_1+\Omega_2\), and define \(S(x):=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\Omega_1\times\Omega_2:x_1+x_2=x\}\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\widehat N(\bar x;\Omega_1+\Omega_2)\subset\bigcup_{(x_1,x_2)\in S(\bar x)+\varepsilon\mathbb B}[(\widehat N(x_1;\Omega_1)+\varepsilon\mathbb B^*)\cap(\widehat N(x_2;\Omega_2)+\varepsilon\mathbb B^*)]\). If \(S\) is inner semicompact at \(\bar x\), then \(N(\bar x;\Omega_1+\Omega_2)\subset\bigcup_{(x_1,x_2)\in S(\bar x)}[N(x_1;\Omega_1)\cap N(x_2;\Omega_2)]\). If for some \((\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\in S(\bar x)\), \(S\) is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x,\bar x_1,\bar x_2)\), then \(N(\bar x;\Omega_1+\Omega_2)\subset N(\bar x_1;\Omega_1)\cap N(\bar x_2;\Omega_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular normal to a Minkowski sum is an approximate common regular normal at a nearby decomposition. Inner semicompactness yields a limiting-normal union rule over exact decompositions, while inner semicontinuity at a selected decomposition yields a single-decomposition inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated fuzzy regular-normal inclusion holds; inner semicompactness of \(S\) gives the union inclusion for limiting normals, and inner semicontinuity at a chosen decomposition gives the single-decomposition inclusion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximation of horizontal Fréchet epigraph normals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asplund-space sequential representation using vanishingly scaled Fréchet subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be Asplund and let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous around \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\). If \((x^*,0)\in\widehat N((\bar x,\varphi(\bar x));\operatorname{epi}\varphi)\), then there exist sequences \(x_k\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x\), \(\lambda_k\downarrow0\), and \(x_k^*\in\lambda_k\widehat\partial\varphi(x_k)\) such that \(\|x_k^*-x^*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every horizontal Fréchet normal to the epigraph of a proper function that is locally lower semicontinuous on an Asplund space is the norm limit of vanishing positive multiples of nearby Fréchet subgradients, with convergence of both points and function values.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper and lower semicontinuous around }\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x_k\overset{\varphi}{\to}\bar x,\ \lambda_k\downarrow0,\ x_k^*\in\lambda_k\widehat\partial\varphi(x_k):\ \|x_k^*-x^*\|\to0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Chain Rule for Mixed Coderivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two closedness and semicontinuity regimes for a composition, with the mappings and solution multifunction defined as in Theorem 3.13.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G,F,S\) be as in Theorem 3.13 and \(\bar z\in(F\circ G)(\bar x)\). (i) Given \(\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z)\), suppose that \(S\) is inner semicontinuous at \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\), that \(\operatorname{gph}F\) and \(\operatorname{gph}G\) are locally closed around \((\bar y,\bar z)\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\), respectively, and that \(F\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar y,\bar z)\). Then \[D_M^*(F\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(0)\subset D_M^*G(\bar x,\bar y)(0).\] (ii) Suppose that \(S\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar z)\), that \(G\) and \(F^{-1}\) satisfy the stated closed-graph conditions for \(x\) near \(\bar x\) and \(z\) near \(\bar z\), respectively, and that \(F\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar y,\bar z)\) for every \(\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z)\). Then \[D_M^*(F\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(0)\subset\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z)}D_M^*G(\bar x,\bar y)(0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under either the fixed-intermediate-point inner-semicontinuity regime or the all-intermediate-points inner-semicompactness regime, the zero-argument mixed coderivative of the composition is contained in the corresponding mixed coderivative of the inner mapping, or in their union over intermediate points.
assumptions_latex: \text{In (i), }\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z)\text{ and }S\text{ is inner semicontinuous at }(\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)
\text{In (i), }\operatorname{gph}F\text{ and }\operatorname{gph}G\text{ are locally closed at the stated points and }F\text{ is Lipschitz-like there}
\text{In (ii), }S\text{ is inner semicompact at }(\bar x,\bar z)
\text{In (ii), the stated closed-graph conditions hold and }F\text{ is Lipschitz-like at every relevant intermediate point}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_M^*(F\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(0)\subset D_M^*G(\bar x,\bar y)(0)\text{ in (i), and }D_M^*(F\circ G)(\bar x,\bar z)(0)\subset\bigcup_{\bar y\in S(\bar x,\bar z)}D_M^*G(\bar x,\bar y)(0)\text{ in (ii).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: PSNC Preservation for Sums of Set-Valued Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PSNC of a pointwise sum under inner semicompactness of decompositions and a mixed-coderivative qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}(F_1+F_2), where F_1 and F_2 have closed graphs for x near \bar x. Define S(x,y)=\{(y_1,y_2)\in Y^2\mid y_i\in F_i(x),\ y_1+y_2=y\}. Suppose S is inner semicompact at (\bar x,\bar y). If, for every (\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y), each F_i is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y_i) and D_M^*F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(0)\cap[-D_M^*F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)(0)]=\{0\}, then F_1+F_2 is PSNC at (\bar x,\bar y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise sum of two locally closed-graph PSNC multifunctions is PSNC when feasible output decompositions are inner semicompact and the two mixed coderivatives at zero have no nonzero opposing element.
assumptions_latex: F_i\text{ has closed graph whenever }x\text{ is near }\bar x,\quad i=1,2
S(x,y)=\{(y_1,y_2)\mid y_i\in F_i(x),\ y_1+y_2=y\}\text{ is inner semicompact at }(\bar x,\bar y)
\forall(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y):\ F_i\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y_i),\ i=1,2
\forall(\bar y_1,\bar y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y):\ D_M^*F_1(\bar x,\bar y_1)(0)\cap[-D_M^*F_2(\bar x,\bar y_2)(0)]=\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_1+F_2\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)
