children.title: Prox-Regular Functions
children.top_down_role: The central nonconvex proximal regularity class.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A uniform local quadratic lower-support inequality defines prox-regularity of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise prox-regularity relative to a limiting subgradient in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is prox-regular at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) if there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(r\ge0\) such that \[f(x')\ge f(x)+\langle v,x'-x\rangle-\frac r2\|x'-x\|^2\] whenever \(\|x-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\), \(\|x'-\bar x\|<\varepsilon\), \(|f(x)-f(\bar x)|<\varepsilon\), and \(v\in\partial f(x)\) satisfies \(\|v-\bar v\|<\varepsilon\). The function is prox-regular at \(\bar x\) when it is prox-regular there for every \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prox-regularity requires nearby limiting subgradients to provide a uniform local quadratic lower support around a specified point-subgradient pair.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Regular Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The point-subgradient definition is consistent with the standard finite-dimensional limiting-subdifferential formulation and the definition content kind fits the Prox-Regular Functions topic. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near \(\bar z=\bar x+\lambda\bar v\), the proximal mapping \(P_\lambda f=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}\) has a single-valued Lipschitz localization with \(P_\lambda f(\bar z)=\bar x\).
review_flags: exact localization theorem and neighborhood hypotheses require an authoritative source
prox-regularity convention must be aligned with the surrounding chapter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local resolvent form for prox-regular, subdifferentially continuous functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\), with prox-regularity modulus \(r\). For every \(\lambda\in(0,1/r)\), there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar z=\bar x+\lambda\bar v\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that the localized inclusion \[x\in V,\qquad z-x\in\lambda\partial f(x)\] has, for each \(z\in U\), a unique solution \(x=P_\lambda f(z)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic, Semianalytic, and Subanalytic Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local definitions for functions, sets, and vector-valued maps in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:U\to\mathbb R\), where \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) is open, is analytic if it is represented by a convergent power series in a neighborhood of every point of \(U\); a vector-valued map is analytic when each component is analytic. A set \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is semianalytic if, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(a\), positive integers \(p,q\), and analytic functions \(f_{ij}\) on \(U\) such that \(X\cap U=\bigcup_{i=1}^{p}\bigcap_{j=1}^{q}X_{ij}\), with every \(X_{ij}\) of the form \(\{x\in U:f_{ij}(x)=0\}\) or \(\{x\in U:f_{ij}(x)<0\}\). It is subanalytic if, for every \(a\), some neighborhood \(U\) satisfies \(X\cap U=\Pi(A)\), where \(A\subset\mathbb R^{n+p}\) is bounded and semianalytic for some \(p\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and \(\Pi(x,y)=x\). A vector-valued map is semianalytic or subanalytic when its graph is so.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analytic functions have local convergent power-series representations. Semianalytic sets are locally finite unions of finite intersections of analytic equality and strict-inequality sets. Subanalytic sets are locally projections of bounded semianalytic sets. Vector-valued maps are classified through their graphs.
assumptions_latex: p,q\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\text{ for the semianalytic representation}
p\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\text{ for the projection representation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated local representations define analytic maps, semianalytic sets, subanalytic sets, and the corresponding graph-defined map classes.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic, semianalytic, and semialgebraic functions and sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local power-series, finite-description, and graph criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be open. A function f:X\to\mathbb{R} is analytic if, for every \bar x\in X, it agrees on a neighborhood of \bar x with a convergent real power series centered at \bar x; every such function is locally Lipschitz continuous. A subset of X is analytic if it has a finite representation by analytic equalities and inequalities. A set is semialgebraic if it is a finite union of sets described by polynomial equalities and strict polynomial inequalities. A set S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n is semianalytic if, for every \bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n, some neighborhood V of \bar x makes S\cap V a finite union of sets described by analytic equalities and strict analytic inequalities. A mapping h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m is semianalytic, respectively semialgebraic, if \operatorname{gph}h\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+m} has the corresponding property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analytic functions have local convergent power-series representations and are locally Lipschitz. Analytic and semialgebraic sets have finite analytic or polynomial descriptions, while semianalytic sets have such analytic descriptions locally. A mapping is semianalytic or semialgebraic when its graph is.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These local-representation, finite-description, and graph criteria define the stated classes, and analytic functions are locally Lipschitz.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Łojasiewicz inequality for subanalytic zero sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform power comparison on a compact subanalytic domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X\subset\mathbb{R}^n be compact and subanalytic, and let \phi,\psi:X\to\mathbb{R} be continuous subanalytic functions. If \phi^{-1}(0)\subseteq\psi^{-1}(0), then there exist \rho>0 and N^*\in\mathbb{N}_{>0} such that \rho|\psi(x)|^{N^*}\le |\phi(x)| for every x\in X. If also \psi^{-1}(0)\subseteq\phi^{-1}(0), then there exist \rho_1,\rho_2>0 and N_1,N_2\in\mathbb{N}_{>0} such that \rho_1|\psi(x)|^{N_1}\le |\phi(x)|\le\rho_2|\psi(x)|^{1/N_2} for every x\in X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact subanalytic set, inclusion of one continuous subanalytic function's zero set in another's yields a uniform power-law comparison. Equality of the zero sets yields two-sided power-law equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\rho>0,\ N^*\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\ \forall x\in X:\ \rho|\psi(x)|^{N^*}\le|\phi(x)|;\quad \phi^{-1}(0)=\psi^{-1}(0)\Rightarrow\text{the stated two-sided power comparison}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sard's Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-value measure-zero theorem for sufficiently differentiable Euclidean maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,m\ge 1\). If \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is of class \(C^k\) with \(k\ge\max\{1,n-m+1\}\), then the set \(\{f(x):\operatorname{rank}f'(x)<m\}\) of critical values of \(f\) has measure zero in \(\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive integers n and m, if a map from R^n to R^m is C^k with k at least the maximum of 1 and n−m+1, then its set of critical values has measure zero in R^m.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{f(x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ \operatorname{rank}f'(x)<m\}\text{ has measure zero in }\mathbb{R}^m.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Measure-Zero Sets, Critical Points, and Critical Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for subsets of Euclidean space and continuously differentiable maps between Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has outer measure zero if, for every \(\epsilon>0\), there exist balls \((B_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}\) such that \(S\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}B_i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\operatorname{vol}(B_i)<\epsilon\). For a \(C^1\) map \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), a point \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is critical if \(\operatorname{rank}f'(x)<m\); a point \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is a critical value if there exists a critical point \(x\) with \(f(x)=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset of Euclidean space has outer measure zero when it can, for every positive epsilon, be covered by countably many balls whose total volume is less than epsilon. For a continuously differentiable map from R^n to R^m, a point is critical when the derivative has rank below m, and a value is critical when it is the image of at least one critical point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ has outer measure zero}\iff \forall\epsilon>0\;\exists(B_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}:S\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}B_i\text{ and }\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\operatorname{vol}(B_i)<\epsilon;\quad x\text{ is critical}\iff\operatorname{rank}f'(x)<m;\quad y\text{ is a critical value}\iff\exists x\,[f(x)=y\land\operatorname{rank}f'(x)<m].

knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Critical-Value Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semialgebraic Sard theorem for continuously differentiable maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a semialgebraic \(C^1\) manifold and let \(F:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be a semialgebraic \(C^1\) map. Define \(\operatorname{Crit}(F)=\{x\in X:\operatorname{rank}DF(x)<m\}\). Then \(F(\operatorname{Crit}(F))\) is semialgebraic and has dimension strictly smaller than \(m\). Consequently it has empty interior and Lebesgue measure zero in \(\mathbb R^m\). For \(m=1\), the set of critical values is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Critical values of a semialgebraic smooth map form a lower-dimensional semialgebraic set; scalar maps therefore have only finitely many critical values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F(\operatorname{Crit}(F))<m\).

notation.meaning: Points where the differential of F is not surjective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the semialgebraic C1 Sard conclusion or scalar finiteness claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Subanalytic Critical-Value Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local subanalytic Sard theorem; global finiteness requires a global or relatively compact setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a subanalytic \(C^1\) manifold and let \(F:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be a subanalytic \(C^1\) map. On every relatively compact subanalytic open subset \(U\subset X\), the set \(F(\{x\in U:\operatorname{rank}DF(x)<m\})\) is subanalytic and has dimension less than \(m\). Hence it has empty interior and measure zero. When \(m=1\), it has finitely many values on each such tame compact localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After relatively compact localization, critical values of a subanalytic smooth map are subanalytic and lower-dimensional; scalar critical values are locally finite.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subset X\) is relatively compact and subanalytic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F(\{x\in U:\operatorname{rank}DF(x)<m\})<m\).

notation.meaning: A relatively compact localization in X.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local subanalytic formulation fits the leaf, but an authoritative locator is required to verify that the stated relative-compactness assumptions suffice for subanalyticity, dimension loss, and scalar finiteness.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Value Regime Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of semialgebraic, subanalytic, and o-minimal Sard regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Semialgebraic maps constitute a definable subclass and admit global dimension statements without boundedness assumptions. Subanalytic maps admit the same local dimension conclusion, while global subanalytic conclusions generally require properness, relative compactness, or global subanalyticity. In any fixed o-minimal structure, a definable \(C^1\) map \(F:X\to\mathbb R^m\) satisfies \(\dim F(\operatorname{Crit}(F))<m\). Thus the three regimes share the lower-dimensional conclusion but differ in closure properties and the hypotheses needed to globalize it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All three tame regimes yield lower-dimensional critical values, but subanalytic global statements require additional compactness or properness conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to\mathbb R^m\) is \(C^1\) in the stated tame category.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F(\operatorname{Crit}(F))<m\), subject to the stated localization requirements.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind suits this comparison leaf, but the distinctions among semialgebraic, local subanalytic, globally subanalytic, and o-minimal regimes require sources for each category.

knowledge_statements.title: Definable Critical-Value Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: O-minimal Sard theorem for definable continuously differentiable maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an o-minimal expansion of the real field. Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a definable \(C^1\) manifold and let \(F:X\to\mathbb R^m\) be definable and \(C^1\). Then the critical-value set \(F(\{x\in X:\operatorname{rank}DF(x)<m\})\) is definable and has dimension strictly less than \(m\). In particular, it is nowhere dense and null in \(\mathbb R^m\); when \(m=1\), it is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an o-minimal structure, classical critical values of a definable smooth map form a definable lower-dimensional set.
assumptions_latex: An o-minimal expansion of \((\mathbb R,+,\cdot)\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F(\{x\in X:\operatorname{rank}DF(x)<m\})<m\).

children.title: Clarke Critical-Value Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Critical-Value Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar locally Lipschitz criticality based on the Clarke generalized gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and let \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz. Its Clarke critical set and Clarke critical-value set are, respectively, \[\operatorname{Crit}_{C}(f)=\{x\in U:0\in\partial_C f(x)\},\qquad \operatorname{CV}_{C}(f)=f(\operatorname{Crit}_{C}(f)).\] Here \(\partial_C f(x)\) is the closed convex hull of all limits of gradients \(\nabla f(x_k)\) at differentiability points \(x_k\to x\). Convexification makes this criticality generally weaker than limiting-subdifferential criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Clarke critical point is one whose convexified generalized gradient contains zero; its image is a Clarke critical value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CV}_{C}(f)=\{f(x):0\in\partial_C f(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized gradient of f at x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vector-Field Representation of the Minimal Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: At a regular measure, the unique minimal subdifferential plan is concentrated on the graph of a tangent vector field.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Nonempty Common Subdifferential Forces Affinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affinity of a finite convex function on a closed convex set possessing a common subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex. If $\widehat{\partial f}(X):=\bigcap_{x\in X}\partial f(x)\ne\emptyset$, then, for every $g\in\widehat{\partial f}(X)$ and all $x_0,x_1\in X$, $f(x_1)=f(x_0)+\langle g,x_1-x_0\rangle$. Consequently, for all $x_0,x_1\in X$ and $\alpha\in[0,1]$, $f((1-\alpha)x_0+\alpha x_1)=(1-\alpha)f(x_0)+\alpha f(x_1)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a finite convex function has a subgradient common to every point of a nonempty closed convex set, then the function is affine on that set, with every common subgradient providing its affine slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall g\in\widehat{\partial f}(X),\ \forall x_0,x_1\in X:\ f(x_1)=f(x_0)+\langle g,x_1-x_0\rangle;\quad \forall\alpha\in[0,1]:\ f((1-\alpha)x_0+\alpha x_1)=(1-\alpha)f(x_0)+\alpha f(x_1).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radial-subdifferential characterizations for generalized PC1 functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three regimes determining radial subgradients and their relation to the Clarke generalized gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) be generalized \(PC^1\) at \(x^0\). Then: (i) if \(\alpha(x^0)<\alpha_r(x^0)\) for every \(r\), then \(\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)=\mathbb{R}^m\); (ii) if, for some fixed selection \(\alpha^i\), equality \(\alpha(x^0)=\alpha_r(x^0)\) holds exactly for \(r\in K_{\operatorname{Supp}(\alpha,\alpha^i)}(x^0)\), while \(\alpha(x^0)<\alpha_r(x^0)\) outside this cone, then \(\nabla\alpha^i(x^0)\in\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)\); and (iii) if \(\alpha\) is continuous on an open neighborhood of \(x^0\), then it is special \(PC^1\), is locally Lipschitz, and \(\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)=\partial_C\alpha(x^0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a generalized PC1 function, strict radial separation makes every vector a radial subgradient. Under a fixed active-selection cone condition, the selected branch gradient is a radial subgradient. If the function is continuous near x0, it is locally Lipschitz and its radial subdifferential equals the Clarke generalized gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\bigl[\forall r,\ \alpha(x^0)<\alpha_r(x^0)\bigr]\Rightarrow\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)=\mathbb{R}^m;\\&\bigl[\alpha(x^0)=\alpha_r(x^0)\iff r\in K_{\operatorname{Supp}(\alpha,\alpha^i)}(x^0)\bigr]\Rightarrow\nabla\alpha^i(x^0)\in\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0);\\&\bigl[\alpha\text{ is continuous near }x^0\bigr]\Rightarrow\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)=\partial_C\alpha(x^0).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke generalized directional derivative and gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and basic representation for a locally Lipschitz real-valued function on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be locally Lipschitz near $x$. For $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, define
\[
f^{\circ}(x;v):=\limsup_{\substack{y\to x\\ \lambda\downarrow0}}\frac{f(y+\lambda v)-f(y)}{\lambda}.
\]
This quantity is finite; as a function of $v$ it is positively homogeneous and subadditive. The Clarke generalized gradient is
\[
\partial f(x):=\{\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^n:f^{\circ}(x;v)\geq\langle v,\zeta\rangle\ \text{for every }v\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
It is nonempty, convex, and compact, and
\[
f^{\circ}(x;v)=\max_{\zeta\in\partial f(x)}\langle\zeta,v\rangle\qquad(v\in\mathbb{R}^n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz function, the Clarke directional derivative is the upper limit of nearby forward difference quotients. It is finite, positively homogeneous, and subadditive. The Clarke generalized gradient consists of all vectors dominated by this directional derivative; it is nonempty, convex, and compact, and its support function equals the generalized directional derivative in every direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f(x)\neq\varnothing\text{ is convex and compact, and }f^{\circ}(x;v)=\max_{\zeta\in\partial f(x)}\langle\zeta,v\rangle\ \forall v\in\mathbb{R}^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke generalized-Jacobian chain rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional image form of the chain rule, including the smooth outer-map equality and scalar-valued specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(W\subset\mathbb R^l\) be nonempty open sets. Suppose \(g:V\to W\) is Lipschitz near \(x\in V\) and \(h:W\to\mathbb R^m\) is Lipschitz near \(g(x)\). Then \(f=h\circ g\) is Lipschitz near \(x\), and for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\partial f(x)v\subset\operatorname{co}\{M_hM_gv:M_h\in\partial h(g(x)),\ M_g\in\partial g(x)\}.\] If \(h\) is continuously differentiable near \(g(x)\), then for every \(v\), \[\partial f(x)v=h'(g(x))\,\partial g(x)v.\] When \(m=1\), both formulas hold with \(v\) omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composition of two mappings that are Lipschitz near the relevant points is Lipschitz near the base point. The action of its Clarke generalized Jacobian on any direction is contained in the convex hull of products of generalized Jacobians of the outer and inner mappings. If the outer mapping is continuously differentiable nearby, this becomes equality with its classical derivative. For a scalar-valued composition, the directional vector may be omitted.
assumptions_latex: V\subset\mathbb R^n,\ W\subset\mathbb R^l\text{ are nonempty and open}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=h\circ g\text{ is Lipschitz near }x,\quad \forall v\in\mathbb R^n:\ \partial f(x)v\subset\operatorname{co}\{M_hM_gv:M_h\in\partial h(g(x)),\ M_g\in\partial g(x)\};\quad h\in C^1\text{ near }g(x)\Rightarrow \partial f(x)v=h'(g(x))\partial g(x)v,\text{ and if }m=1\text{ then }v\text{ may be omitted}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product relations for partial and joint subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A first-order blockwise generalized-differentiation result under additive separability of the B-derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathcal O_x\times\mathcal O_y\to\mathbb R\) be B-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar y)\), where \(\mathcal O_x\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\mathcal O_y\subset\mathbb R^m\) are open, and suppose \(\phi'((\bar x,\bar y);(u,v))=\phi_x'((\bar x,\bar y);u)+\phi_y'((\bar x,\bar y);v)\) for every \((u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}\). Then \(\widehat\partial\phi(\bar x,\bar y)=\widehat\partial_x\phi(\bar x,\bar y)\times\widehat\partial_y\phi(\bar x,\bar y)\). If the two partial functions \(\phi(\cdot,\bar y)\) and \(\phi(\bar x,\cdot)\) are Clarke regular at \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y\), respectively, then \(\partial_{C,x}\phi(\bar x,\bar y)\times\partial_{C,y}\phi(\bar x,\bar y)\subseteq\partial_C\phi(\bar x,\bar y)\); this inclusion is an equality if \(\phi\) is also Clarke regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a B-differentiable two-block function whose directional derivative splits additively across the blocks, the joint regular subdifferential equals the Cartesian product of the two partial regular subdifferentials. If both partial functions are Clarke regular, the product of their partial Clarke subdifferentials is contained in the joint Clarke subdifferential; joint Clarke regularity strengthens this inclusion to equality.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal O_x\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ and }\mathcal O_y\subset\mathbb R^m\text{ are open}
\phi:\mathcal O_x\times\mathcal O_y\to\mathbb R\text{ is B-differentiable at }(\bar x,\bar y)
\forall (u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n+m},\quad \phi'((\bar x,\bar y);(u,v))=\phi_x'((\bar x,\bar y);u)+\phi_y'((\bar x,\bar y);v)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\partial\phi(\bar x,\bar y)=\widehat\partial_x\phi(\bar x,\bar y)\times\widehat\partial_y\phi(\bar x,\bar y);\quad [\phi(\cdot,\bar y)\text{ and }\phi(\bar x,\cdot)\text{ Clarke regular}]\Rightarrow \partial_{C,x}\phi\times\partial_{C,y}\phi\subseteq\partial_C\phi,\text{ with equality if }\phi\text{ is Clarke regular at }(\bar x,\bar y).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic properties of B-, Clarke-, and C-subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, compactness, continuity, inclusions, and smooth consistency for locally Lipschitz mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open and \(f:V\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz. For every \(x\in V\), \(\partial_Bf(x)\) is nonempty and compact; \(\partial f(x)\) and \(\partial_Cf(x)\) are nonempty, compact, and convex. The mappings \(\partial_Bf\), \(\partial f\), and \(\partial_Cf\) are locally bounded and upper semicontinuous, and \[\partial_Bf(x)\subset\partial f(x)\subset\partial_Cf(x).\] If \(f\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(x\), then \[\partial_Cf(x)=\partial f(x)=\partial_Bf(x)=\{f'(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every point, the B-subdifferential is nonempty and compact, while the Clarke and C-subdifferentials are additionally convex. All three set-valued mappings are locally bounded and upper semicontinuous, with the B-subdifferential contained in the Clarke generalized Jacobian and that contained in the C-subdifferential. Near a continuously differentiable point, all three reduce to the singleton classical Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_Bf(x)\neq\varnothing\text{ is compact};\quad \partial f(x),\partial_Cf(x)\neq\varnothing\text{ are compact and convex};\quad \partial_Bf(x)\subset\partial f(x)\subset\partial_Cf(x),\text{ with local boundedness and upper semicontinuity; if }f\in C^1\text{ near }x,\ \partial_Bf(x)=\partial f(x)=\partial_Cf(x)=\{f'(x)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Properties of the Relative Generalized Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure, boundary behavior, nonemptiness, and upper semicontinuity for a locally Lipschitz function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If f is Lipschitz near x, then \left.\partial\right|_S f(x) is a closed subset of \partial f(x). Moreover, x\in\operatorname{int}S implies \left.\partial\right|_S f(x)=\partial f(x); if (x+\varepsilon B)\cap S=\varnothing for some \varepsilon>0, then \left.\partial\right|_S f(x)=\varnothing; if x\in\operatorname{cl}S, then \left.\partial\right|_S f(x)\neq\varnothing. The mapping \left.\partial\right|_S f is upper semicontinuous at x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For f Lipschitz near x, the relative generalized gradient is a closed subset of the generalized gradient. It equals the full generalized gradient at interior points of S, is empty when a neighborhood of x misses S, is nonempty when x lies in the closure of S, and is upper semicontinuous at x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization and closedness properties of the Clarke subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties of the Clarke subdifferential of a locally Lipschitz function on a Banach space, including the additional finite-dimensional upper-semicontinuity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a Banach space and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz near the points considered. Then: (a) \(\zeta\in\partial f(x)\iff f^{\circ}(x;v)\ge\langle\zeta,v\rangle\) for every \(v\in X\). (b) If \(x_i\to x\), \(\zeta_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), and \(\zeta\) is a weak-star cluster point of \((\zeta_i)\), then \(\zeta\in\partial f(x)\); hence \(\partial f\) is weak-star closed. (c) \(\partial f(x)=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\bigcup_{y\in x+\delta B_X}\partial f(y)\). (d) If \(X\) is finite-dimensional, then \(\partial f\) is upper semicontinuous at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional belongs to the Clarke subdifferential at x exactly when it is dominated by the Clarke generalized directional derivative in every direction. The subdifferential mapping has a weak-star closed graph, its value at x is recovered by intersecting the unions of its values over all neighborhoods of x, and in finite dimensions it is upper semicontinuous at x.
assumptions_latex: f:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is locally Lipschitz near the points considered}
\zeta\text{ is a weak-star cluster point of }(\zeta_i)\text{ for part (b)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \zeta\in\partial f(x)\iff \forall v\in X,\ f^{\circ}(x;v)\ge\langle\zeta,v\rangle;\quad \operatorname{Gr}(\partial f)\text{ is weak-star closed};\quad \partial f(x)=\bigcap_{\delta>0}\bigcup_{y\in x+\delta B_X}\partial f(y);\quad \dim X<\infty\Rightarrow\partial f\text{ is u.s.c. at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calculus and geometry of the radial subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness, convexity, scaling, sum inclusions, boundedness, and a directional support bound for generalized PC1 functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For generalized \(PC^1\) functions at \(x^0\), the radial subdifferential is closed and convex; for every \(\lambda>0\), \(\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}(\lambda\alpha)(x^0)=\lambda\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)\); \(\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}(\alpha^1+\alpha^2)(x^0)\supseteq\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha^1(x^0)+\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha^2(x^0)\); and, for every finite family and \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha^i(x^0)\subseteq\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}(\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha^i)(x^0)\). If \(\alpha\) is continuous at \(x^0\), then \(\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)\) is bounded. Moreover, if \(r^0\neq0\) and \(\alpha(x^0)=\alpha_{r^0}(x^0)\), then \[\mathrm d\alpha(x^0;r^0)\geq\sup\{d^\top r^0:d\in\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The radial subdifferential of generalized PC1 functions is closed and convex, is positively homogeneous, and satisfies superadditive sum inclusions. It is bounded when the function is continuous at the point, and its support in an equality direction is bounded above by the corresponding directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: r^0\neq0\text{ and }\alpha(x^0)=\alpha_{r^0}(x^0)\text{ for the support bound}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)\text{ is closed and convex, obeys the stated positive-scaling and sum rules, is bounded if }\alpha\text{ is continuous at }x^0,\text{ and }\mathrm d\alpha(x^0;r^0)\geq\sup_{d\in\partial_{\mathrm{rad}}\alpha(x^0)}d^\top r^0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible-point selected-subgradient oracle model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information model for minimizing a locally Lipschitz objective under locally Lipschitz inequality constraints; full subdifferentials and infeasible-point evaluations are not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(F_i(x)\le 0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where \(f,F_i:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R\) are locally Lipschitz. Define \(F(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}F_i(x)\) for \(m\ge1\), and \(F(x)=0\) for \(m=0\), with \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:F(x)\le0\}\). The oracle supplies, at each \(x\in S\), \(f(x)\) and one selected subgradient \(g_f(x)\in\partial f(x)\), and, when \(m\ge1\), corresponding constraint information \(F_i(x)\) and one selected \(g_{F_i}(x)\in\partial F_i(x)\) for every \(i\). No additional property of the selected subgradients is assumed; objective information need not be available outside \(S\). When explicitly imposed for convenience, these selections may instead be defined on all of \(\mathbb R^N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a constrained problem whose objective and constraint functions are locally Lipschitz on Euclidean space, feasibility is represented by the maximum constraint violation, with the unconstrained case assigned zero violation. At each feasible point, the information routine returns the objective and one arbitrary selected subgradient, together with corresponding information for every constraint. It need not expose the full subdifferentials or provide objective information at infeasible points. A stronger, temporary convention may extend the selected subgradients to every point in the space.
assumptions_latex: f,F_i:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R\text{ are locally Lipschitz for }i=1,\ldots,m.
\forall x\in S,\quad g_f(x)\in\partial f(x),\qquad g_{F_i}(x)\in\partial F_i(x)\ (i=1,\ldots,m).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Optimization may proceed using only feasible-point function information and one unrestricted selected subgradient per available problem function, without access to complete subdifferentials or mandatory objective evaluations on }\mathbb R^N\setminus S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: B-subdifferential, Clarke generalized Jacobian, and C-subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions for a vector-valued mapping that is Lipschitz near the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\) be open, \(x\in V\), and let \(f:V\to\mathbb R^m\) be Lipschitz continuous near \(x\). If \(D_f\) is the set where \(f\) is differentiable, then \[\partial_B f(x):=\{M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\exists (x_k)\subset D_f,\ x_k\to x,\ f'(x_k)\to M\}.\] The Clarke generalized Jacobian is \(\partial f(x):=\operatorname{co}(\partial_B f(x))\), and Qi's C-subdifferential is \(\partial_C f(x):=\partial f_1(x)\times\cdots\times\partial f_m(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a mapping Lipschitz near x, the B-subdifferential consists of all limits of classical Jacobians along differentiability points approaching x. The Clarke generalized Jacobian is its convex hull, while Qi's C-subdifferential is the Cartesian product of the Clarke subdifferentials of the component functions.
assumptions_latex: f:V\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is Lipschitz continuous near }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_B f(x)=\{M:\exists x_k\in D_f,\ x_k\to x,\ f'(x_k)\to M\},\quad \partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}(\partial_Bf(x)),\quad \partial_Cf(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak and strong approximate-Jacobian J-semismoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional semismoothness relative to an approximate Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m have approximate Jacobian \partial^*f. It is weakly \partial^*f-J-semismooth at x if it is continuous near x and \[\sup_{M\in\overline{\operatorname{co}}\,\partial^*f(x+s)}\|f(x+s)-f(x)-Ms\|=o(\|s\|)\quad(s\to0).\] It is \partial^*f-J-semismooth at x if, in addition, f is B-differentiable at x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map is weakly J-semismooth relative to an approximate Jacobian when it is continuous near the point and every matrix in the closed convex hull of the nearby approximate Jacobians gives a linearization error that is little-o of the step norm. It is J-semismooth when it is also B-differentiable at the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is weakly }\partial^*f\text{-J-semismooth at }x\iff f\text{ is continuous near }x\text{ and }\sup_{M\in\overline{\operatorname{co}}\partial^*f(x+s)}\|f(x+s)-f(x)-Ms\|=o(\|s\|);\quad f\text{ is }\partial^*f\text{-J-semismooth at }x\iff f\text{ is B-differentiable at }x\text{ and weakly }\partial^*f\text{-J-semismooth at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness and Upper Semicontinuity of the Clarke Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic mapping properties for the Clarke subdifferential of a locally Lipschitz function on finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz. Then: (i) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^N\), \(\partial^C f(x)\) is nonempty, convex, and compact; (ii) for every bounded \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^N\), the set \(\bigcup_{y\in B}\partial^C f(y)\) is bounded; and (iii) if \(y^j\to x\), \(g^j\in\partial^C f(y^j)\), and a subsequence of \(g^j\) converges to \(g\), then \(g\in\partial^C f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Clarke subdifferential has nonempty compact convex values, is bounded over bounded subsets, and has a closed-graph or upper-semicontinuity property under convergent base points and subgradient subsequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x,\ \partial^C f(x)\text{ is nonempty, convex, compact};\quad \forall B\text{ bounded},\ \bigcup_{y\in B}\partial^C f(y)\text{ is bounded};\quad y^j\to x,\ g^j\in\partial^C f(y^j),\ g^{j_k}\to g\Rightarrow g\in\partial^C f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential inclusion on a constant convex set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior invariance for a convex function constant and finite on a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:X\to\overline{\mathbb R} be convex and suppose that f is constant and finite on a convex set S. For every x\in S and x_0\in\operatorname{ri}S, \partial f(x_0)\subseteq\partial f(x). Consequently, \partial f(\cdot) is constant on \operatorname{ri}S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a convex function has one finite constant value on a convex set, every subgradient at a relative-interior point of that set is also a subgradient at every point of the set. Hence the subdifferential is constant throughout the relative interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in S\;\forall x_0\in\operatorname{ri}S,\quad \partial f(x_0)\subseteq\partial f(x),\qquad \partial f\text{ is constant on }\operatorname{ri}S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Composition and Finite-Sum Rules for Convex Subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rules for globally finite convex functions, without additional qualification conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R} is convex, A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, and F(x)=h(Ax), then \partial F(x)=A^\top\partial h(Ax) for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n. If f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} are convex for i=1,\ldots,m and F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i, then \partial F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x) for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite convex function composed with a linear map, the subdifferential is the transpose image of the original subdifferential. The subdifferential of a finite sum of finite convex functions is the Minkowski sum of their subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial(h\circ A)(x)=A^\top\partial h(Ax),\qquad \partial\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial f_i(x)\quad\forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform continuous approximation of a subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a domain-uniform, nested, Hausdorff-continuous family recovering the exact subdifferential pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\{\mathcal A_\varepsilon f(\cdot)\}_{\varepsilon>0}\) is a uniform continuous approximation of \(\partial f\) on \(X\) if: (i) for every \(\varepsilon,\mu>0\) there exists \(\tau>0\) such that, for every \(x\in X\), \(\partial f(x+\bar B(0;\tau))\subseteq\mathcal A_\varepsilon f(x)+\bar B(0;\mu)\); (ii) for every \(x\in X\) and \(0<\varepsilon_1<\varepsilon_2\), \(\mathcal A_{\varepsilon_1}f(x)\subseteq\mathcal A_{\varepsilon_2}f(x)\); (iii) for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(x\mapsto\mathcal A_\varepsilon f(x)\) is Hausdorff continuous on \(X\); and (iv) for every \(x\in X\), \(\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\mathcal A_\varepsilon f(x)=\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform continuous subdifferential approximation uniformly covers nearby exact subgradients up to any prescribed error, is nested in its positive tolerance, is Hausdorff continuous in the base point, and recovers the exact subdifferential by intersection over all positive tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \{\mathcal A_\varepsilon f(\cdot)\}_{\varepsilon>0}\text{ is a family of set-valued mappings on }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{\mathcal A_\varepsilon f\}_{\varepsilon>0}\text{ is a uniform continuous approximation of }\partial f\text{ on }X\iff\text{conditions (i)--(iv) hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate-Jacobian J-semismoothness of order α

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1\) and \(f_2\) be closed convex functions, let \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\ge 0\), and define \(f=\alpha_1f_1+\alpha_2f_2\). Then \(f\) is closed and convex, and for every
\[
x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)=\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f_1)\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f_2),
\]
one has
\[
\partial f(x)=\alpha_1\partial f_1(x)+\alpha_2\partial f_2(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative weighted sum of two closed convex functions is closed and convex, and at every point in the stated common interior of their domains its subdifferential is the corresponding weighted Minkowski sum of the component subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is closed and convex},\qquad \partial f(x)=\alpha_1\partial f_1(x)+\alpha_2\partial f_2(x)

children.title: Partly Smooth Functions

knowledge_statements.title: Partly Smooth Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential partial smoothness at a point-subgradient pair relative to a manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\) containing \(\bar x\), when: \(f|_M\) is \(C^2\) near \(\bar x\); \(f\) is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\); \(\operatorname{par}\partial f(\bar x)=N_M(\bar x)\); and \(\partial f\) is inner semicontinuous at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\) for \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partly smooth function is smooth along an active manifold, sharp transversely, prox-regular, and has a subgradient mapping continuous along that manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) relative to \(M\).

notation.meaning: Linear subspace parallel to the affine hull of C.
Normal space to M at the reference point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but partial-smoothness conventions vary. A source must verify the selected prox-regularity, sharpness, and relative inner-semicontinuity conditions at the point-subgradient pair.

children.title: Partly Smooth Sets
children.top_down_role: Sets with locally stable active-manifold structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Partly Smooth Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set partial smoothness induced by the indicator function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(\bar x\in C\), and let \(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\). The set \(C\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\), relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\subset C\) through \(\bar x\), precisely when its indicator \(\delta_C\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) relative to \(M\). Equivalently, this requires prox-regularity at the pair, normal sharpness \(\operatorname{par}N_C(\bar x)=N_M(\bar x)\), and relative inner continuity of \(N_C\) along \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is partly smooth when its indicator is partly smooth, giving a smooth active manifold, transverse sharpness, and stable normals along it.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in C\) and \(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\).
\(M\subset C\) is a \(C^2\) manifold through \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is partly smooth relative to \(M\) if and only if \(\delta_C\) is partly smooth relative to \(M\) at \((\bar x,\bar v)\).

notation.meaning: Indicator function of C, equal to zero on C and infinity otherwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition appropriately reduces set partial smoothness to indicator-function partial smoothness, but the claimed equivalent normal-cone conditions depend on the unsourced function-level convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Smoothness of a Closed Convex Cone Along Its Lineality Space

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\subset\mathbf E\) is a closed convex cone, then \(K\) is partly smooth relative to \(K\cap(-K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every closed convex cone is partly smooth relative to its lineality space, namely its intersection with its negative.
assumptions_latex: K\subset\mathbf E\text{ is a closed convex cone}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is partly smooth relative to }K\cap(-K)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partly Smooth Closed Set Relative to a Manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines set partial smoothness through tangential regularity, normal-space sharpness, and inner continuity of normals along the manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed set \(S\subset\mathbf E\) is partly smooth relative to a manifold \(M\subset S\) if, for every \(x\in M\), the set \(S\) is tangentially regular at \(x\), \(N_M(x)=N_S(x)-N_S(x)\), and, for every \(y\in N_S(x)\) and every sequence \(x_r\in M\) converging to \(x\), there exist normals \(y_r\in N_S(x_r)\) converging to \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed set is partly smooth relative to a contained manifold when it is tangentially regular along that manifold, its normal-cone difference equals the manifold normal space, and normals can be approximated along every convergent sequence in the manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in M:\ S\text{ is tangentially regular at }x,\ N_M(x)=N_S(x)-N_S(x),\ \forall y\in N_S(x),\ \forall(x_r)\subset M,\ x_r\to x,\ \exists y_r\in N_S(x_r),\ y_r\to y

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pullback Chain Rule for Partly Smooth Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a transversality condition under which partial smoothness is preserved by a continuously differentiable inverse image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf Y\) be a Euclidean space, let \(h:\mathbf E\to\mathbf Y\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(x\in\mathbf E\), and let the closed set \(R\subset\mathbf Y\) be partly smooth relative to a manifold \(M\) containing \(h(x)\). If \[\nabla h(x)\mathbf E-T_M(h(x))=\mathbf Y,\] then there exists an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) such that \(h^{-1}(M)\cap U\) is a manifold and \(h^{-1}(R)\) is partly smooth relative to that manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a continuously differentiable map is transverse at x to the active manifold of a partly smooth closed set, then locally the inverse image of the manifold is a manifold and the inverse image of the set is partly smooth relative to it.
assumptions_latex: R\subset\mathbf Y\text{ is closed and partly smooth relative to }M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni x\text{ open}:\ h^{-1}(M)\cap U\text{ is a manifold and }h^{-1}(R)\text{ is partly smooth relative to }h^{-1}(M)\cap U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial smoothness of a smooth inequality system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A linear-independence criterion producing the local active manifold of a smooth inequality-defined set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $I$ be finite, let $g_i:\mathbf E\to\mathbf R$ be continuously differentiable around $\bar x$, and define $S=\{x\in\mathbf E:g_i(x)\leq0\ \forall i\in I\}$ and $I(x)=\{i\in I:g_i(x)=0\}$. If $\bar x\in S$ and $\{\nabla g_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}$ is linearly independent, then some open neighborhood $U$ of $\bar x$ has the property that $M=\{x\in U:I(x)=I(\bar x)\}$ is a manifold and $S$ is partly smooth at $\bar x$ relative to $M$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many smooth inequalities, linear independence of the gradients active at a feasible point makes the nearby constant-active-set stratum a manifold, relative to which the feasible set is partly smooth at that point.

S=\{x\in\mathbf E:g_i(x)\leq0\ \forall i\in I\},\quad \bar x\in S
\{\nabla g_i(\bar x):i\in I(\bar x)\}\text{ is linearly independent}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,U\ni\bar x\text{ open such that }M=\{x\in U:I(x)=I(\bar x)\}\text{ is a manifold and }S\text{ is partly smooth at }\bar x\text{ relative to }M.

knowledge_statements.title: Partly Smooth Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial smoothness of a set-valued mapping through its graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set-valued mapping \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), call \(F\) partly smooth at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(G\subset\mathbb R^{n+m}\) when \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is partly smooth there relative to \(G\), for a specified graph normal \((\bar u,-\bar v)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\). Thus graph-restricted behavior is smooth, graph normals are sharp transverse to \(G\), and the graph-normal mapping is continuous along \(G\) at the reference normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued mapping is partly smooth when its graph is a partly smooth set relative to a smooth active graph manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a \(C^2\) manifold through \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is partly smooth at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to \(G\) exactly when \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is partly smooth there for \((\bar u,-\bar v)\).

notation.meaning: Graph of the set-valued mapping F.
Specified normal to the graph at the reference pair.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: graphical reduction of partial smoothness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-based definition fits the mapping leaf, but the terminology, selected graph-normal parameterization, and equivalence with partial smoothness of the graph require an authoritative source.

children.title: Partly Smooth Operators

knowledge_statements.title: Partly Smooth Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-based partial smoothness for operators on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) be an operator on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}T\). Relative to a specified graph normal \((\bar u,-\bar v)\), the operator is partly smooth at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(G\subset H\times H\) when its graph is prox-regular at the reference pair and normal, \(\operatorname{par}N_{\operatorname{gph}T}(\bar x,\bar y)=N_G(\bar x,\bar y)\), and the graph-normal mapping is inner semicontinuous along \(G\) for \((\bar u,-\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partly smooth operator has a prox-regular graph with a smooth active manifold, sharp transverse normals, and stable graph normals along that manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is partly smooth at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) relative to \(G\).

notation.meaning: Active manifold in the product space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the operator leaf, but no source establishes this operator-specific convention or distinguishes it from the adjacent partly smooth mapping notion.

children.title: Graphical Partial Smoothness

knowledge_statements.title: Graphical Partial Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial smoothness formulated intrinsically for a graph and a selected normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closed graphical set \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) is graphically partly smooth at \(\bar z\in Q\) for \(\bar w\in N_Q(\bar z)\), relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(G\subset Q\), when \(Q\) is prox-regular at \(\bar z\) for \(\bar w\), \(\operatorname{par}N_Q(\bar z)=N_G(\bar z)\), and \(N_Q\) is inner semicontinuous at \(\bar z\) relative to \(G\) for \(\bar w\). The manifold \(G\) then records the locally smooth graph geometry exposed by the chosen normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graphical partial smoothness means a graph has a prox-regular active manifold, matching transverse normal space, and stable normals along that manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar z\in Q\) and \(\bar w\in N_Q(\bar z)\).
\(G\subset Q\) is a \(C^2\) manifold through \(\bar z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is graphically partly smooth at \(\bar z\) for \(\bar w\) relative to \(G\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: partial smoothness of a graphical set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is locally appropriate, but graphical partial-smoothness variants are not standardized; the exact prox-regularity, sharpness, and continuity conditions need a specific source.

children.title: Active Manifolds
children.top_down_role: Distinguished smooth pieces carrying stable local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiable manifold associated with a function and a selected subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), and let \(M\) be a \(C^2\) manifold through \(\bar x\). The manifold \(M\) is active at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) if \(f\) is partly smooth there relative to \(M\) and \(M\) is locally identifiable: whenever \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(v_k\to\bar v\), and \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), one has \(x_k\in M\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active manifold witnesses partial smoothness and eventually contains every nearby point carrying a subgradient near the selected one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\) in \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) implies \(x_k\in M\) eventually.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement fits the active-manifold leaf, but a source must verify that this taxonomy's active-manifold notion requires both partial smoothness and the stated sequential identifiability condition.

children.title: Active Strata
children.top_down_role: Distinguished members of a stratification carrying local variational structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Strata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiable stratum for a selected limiting subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be stratifiable, let \(\mathcal S\) be a \(C^2\) stratification compatible with its domain, and let \(S\in\mathcal S\) contain \(\bar x\). For \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), the stratum \(S\) is active at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) if it is locally identifiable for \(\partial f\): every sequence \((x_k,v_k)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) converging to \((\bar x,\bar v)\) satisfies \(x_k\in S\) eventually. If partial smoothness also holds relative to \(S\), the active stratum is an active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active stratum is the unique local smooth piece eventually selected by all nearby graph points of the subdifferential near a chosen pair.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is a \(C^2\) stratification compatible with \(\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\) in \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) implies \(x_k\in S\) eventually.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed identifiability notion is plausible, but terminology varies and no source supports it. The plain statement additionally asserts uniqueness, which neither the LaTeX statement nor the assumptions establish.

children.title: Manifold–Stratum Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Conditions and boundaries governing when active manifolds coincide with active strata.

knowledge_statements.title: Manifold–Stratum Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local correspondence between a partly smooth manifold and a compatible smooth stratification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let \(\mathcal S\) be a local \(C^2\)-stratification of \(\operatorname{dom}f\). If \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\)-manifold \(M\), and the stratum \(S\in\mathcal S\) containing \(\bar x\) is compatible with that partial-smoothness structure, then for some neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), \[M\cap U=S\cap U.\] Consequently, \(T_M(x)=T_S(x)\) and \(N_M(x)=N_S(x)\) for every \(x\in M\cap U\); hence the active manifold and active stratum encode the same local geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a compatible smooth stratification, the partly smooth active manifold is locally the stratum containing the reference point, with identical tangent and normal spaces.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(f\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\)-manifold \(M\).
\(\mathcal S\) is locally compatible with the partial-smoothness structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\cap U=S\cap U\), with \(T_M(x)=T_S(x)\) and \(N_M(x)=N_S(x)\) locally.

notation.meaning: active manifold of the partly smooth function
tangent and normal spaces of the manifold

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard local interpretation of compatible stratified partial smoothness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed local equality of the active manifold and stratum depends on an unspecified compatibility hypothesis. An authoritative partial-smoothness/stratification result with an exact locator is needed to determine sufficient hypotheses.

children.title: Transverse Sharpness
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth growth and separation transverse to an active structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Transverse Sharpness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of a nonsmooth function in directions normal to its active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, let \(M\subset X\) be a \(C^2\)-manifold through \(\bar x\), and suppose \(\partial f(\bar x)\neq\varnothing\). The function is transversely sharp at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\) when \[\operatorname{par}\partial f(\bar x)=N_M(\bar x)=T_M(\bar x)^{\perp},\] where \(\operatorname{par}C=\operatorname{span}(C-C)\). Thus all first-order variation among subgradients occurs precisely in directions normal to the active manifold, while tangent directions contain no subgradient ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transverse sharpness means that differences of subgradients span exactly the normal space of the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{par}\partial f(\bar x)=N_M(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: parallel subspace spanned by differences of points of C
normal space to M at the reference point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard sharpness clause in finite-dimensional partial smoothness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula is a standard sharpness clause in some formulations of partial smoothness, but no cited source fixes the subdifferential convention or confirms that this exact condition is called transverse sharpness.

children.title: Active Normal Spaces
children.top_down_role: Normal geometry associated with the active manifold or stratum.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Normal Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal spaces associated with a smooth active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a \(C^1\)-embedded manifold in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space \(X\), and let \(x\in M\). Its active normal space at \(x\) is \[N_M(x):=T_M(x)^{\perp}=\{v\in X:\langle v,d\rangle=0\text{ for every }d\in T_M(x)\}.\] If locally \(M=\{z:h(z)=0\}\), where \(h:X\to\mathbb R^m\) is \(C^1\) and \(Dh(x)\) has full row rank, then \[N_M(x)=\operatorname{range}Dh(x)^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active normal space is the orthogonal complement of the active manifold’s tangent space; for regular equations, it is the range of the adjoint Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a \(C^1\)-embedded manifold in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_M(x)=T_M(x)^{\perp}\), and under a regular level-set representation, \(N_M(x)=\operatorname{range}Dh(x)^*\).

notation.meaning: tangent space to M at x
adjoint of the derivative of h at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Euclidean embedded-manifold normal-space definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Euclidean normal-space formulas are standard and the definition fits the leaf, but the record contains no citation with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator.

children.title: Sharpness–Normal Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Alignment between transverse nonsmoothness and active normal geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness–Normal Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between subgradient variability and active-manifold normal geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\)-manifold \(M\). Sharpness–normal compatibility requires \[\operatorname{par}\partial f(\bar x)=N_M(\bar x).\] Equivalently, for any \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\), \[\operatorname{aff}\partial f(\bar x)=\bar v+N_M(\bar x).\] Hence the affine hull of the subdifferential is a translate of the active normal space, and its orthogonal complement is the active tangent space \(T_M(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine subgradient geometry is compatible with the active manifold when its direction space equals the manifold’s normal space.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{aff}\partial f(\bar x)=\bar v+N_M(\bar x)\) for every \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard affine-hull reformulation of partial-smoothness sharpness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-hull reformulation is algebraically consistent with the stated parallel-space equality, but a source is needed to confirm the partial-smoothness hypotheses and limiting-subdifferential convention.

children.title: Smooth Active Restrictions
