knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Active Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smoothness of a nonsmooth function after restriction to its active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(M\subset X\) be a \(C^p\)-embedded manifold with \(p\geq2\), and let \(\bar x\in M\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). The active restriction is smooth at \(\bar x\) when there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) in \(M\) such that \(f|_U:U\to\mathbb R\) is \(C^p\). Equivalently, in every \(C^p\) chart \(\phi:V\subset\mathbb R^{\dim M}\to U\), the coordinate function \(f\circ\phi\) is \(C^p\) on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsmooth function has a smooth active restriction when its restriction to the active manifold is smooth in local manifold coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f|_U\) is \(C^p\) on a relative neighborhood \(U\subset M\) of \(\bar x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard smooth-restriction clause of partial smoothness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chart characterization is standard and the condition kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the smooth-restriction clause.

children.title: Constant-Rank Active Geometry
children.top_down_role: Rank-stable differential structure along active manifolds or strata.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Rank Active Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local constant-rank representation of an active manifold by smooth equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:U\subset X\to Y\) be \(C^p\), with \(p\geq1\), between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces. Suppose \(\operatorname{rank}Dh(z)=r\) on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and set \(M=\{z\in U:h(z)=h(\bar x)\}\). Then, after possibly shrinking \(U\), \(M\) is a \(C^p\)-manifold of codimension \(r\), and for every \(x\in M\cap U\), \[T_M(x)=\ker Dh(x),\qquad N_M(x)=\operatorname{range}Dh(x)^*.\] This level-set representation is the constant-rank model of the local active geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-rank defining map makes its local level set a smooth active manifold whose tangent and normal spaces come from the Jacobian kernel and adjoint range.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is \(C^p\) on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
\(Dh\) has constant finite rank \(r\) near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is locally a \(C^p\)-manifold with \(T_M(x)=\ker Dh(x)\) and \(N_M(x)=\operatorname{range}Dh(x)^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constant-rank level-set representation and tangent/normal formulas are standard, but the record supplies no exact constant-rank theorem locator.

children.title: Restriction–Rank Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between smooth restriction geometry and locally stable rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction–Rank Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of a smooth active restriction with a constant-rank manifold representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \(\bar x\in X\), and let \(M\) be locally represented by \(h(x)=h(\bar x)\), where \(h:X\to Y\) is \(C^2\) and \(Dh\) has constant rank near \(\bar x\). Suppose \(f|_M\) is \(C^2\). Restriction–rank compatibility holds when, for every \(x\in M\) near \(\bar x\) and every local \(C^2\) extension \(\widetilde f\) satisfying \(\widetilde f|_M=f|_M\), \[\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)=P_{T_M(x)}\nabla\widetilde f(x),\qquad T_M(x)=\ker Dh(x).\] The projected gradient is independent of the chosen extension because the gradients of any two such extensions differ by an element of \(N_M(x)=\operatorname{range}Dh(x)^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smooth restricted gradient agrees with the projection of any smooth ambient extension’s gradient onto the kernel of the constant-rank Jacobian and is independent of the chosen extension.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has a local \(C^2\) constant-rank level-set representation \(h(x)=h(\bar x)\).
\(f|_M\) is \(C^2\), and \(\widetilde f\) is any local \(C^2\) extension of that restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)=P_{T_M(x)}\nabla\widetilde f(x)\), independently of \(\widetilde f\).

notation.meaning: Riemannian gradient of the restriction of f to M
orthogonal projector onto the tangent space of M at x
local smooth ambient extension of the restriction
adjoint of the derivative of h at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard extension-independence property of manifold gradients
exact differential-geometric source with locator required

children.title: Active-Manifold Identification Principle
children.top_down_role: Finite identification from partial smoothness, prox-regularity, and compatible nondegeneracy.

children.title: Primal-Dual Proximal Identification Family
children.top_down_role: Identification through convergent primal-dual or proximal information.

children.title: Subgradient Identification
children.top_down_role: Active-structure identification through convergent primal-subgradient information.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential identification theorem for a partly smooth function under nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\). Suppose \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\)-manifold \(M\), and \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\). If \((x_k,v_k)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), \[(x_k,v_k,f(x_k))\to(\bar x,\bar v,f(\bar x)),\] then there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for every \(k\geq K\). Thus convergent, nondegenerate subgradient pairs finitely identify the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradient pairs converging to a nondegenerate partly smooth pair eventually have all primal points on the active manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
\(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in M\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard identifiability theorem for partly smooth prox-regular functions
exact theorem and hypothesis set require authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a substantive identification theorem. The exact prox-regularity, subdifferential-continuity, partial-smoothness, function-value convergence, and nondegeneracy hypotheses require an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Proximal Identification
children.top_down_role: Active-structure identification through proximal points, residuals, or certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-manifold identification by nearby proximal points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfy the hypotheses of subgradient identification at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) relative to \(M\), with \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x)\). Choose \(\gamma>0\) so that the proximal mapping is single-valued near \(\bar y=\bar x+\gamma\bar v\). If \(y_k\to\bar y\) and \[x_k=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(y_k),\qquad v_k=\gamma^{-1}(y_k-x_k)\to\bar v,\] then \(x_k\to\bar x\), and there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for all \(k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearby proximal points whose residual subgradients converge nondegenerately eventually lie on the partly smooth active manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) satisfies subgradient-identification hypotheses at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) relative to \(M\).
\(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}\) is single-valued near \(\bar x+\gamma\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in M\).

notation.meaning: proximal mapping of f with parameter gamma

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal optimality reduces identification to convergent subgradient pairs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem needs a source confirming the required proximal localization, the relation \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\bar y)=\bar x\), continuity near \(\bar y\), and the admissible range of \(\gamma\).

children.title: Primal–Dual Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification interfaces coupling primal convergence with compatible dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous identification of primal and dual active manifolds for convex conjugate pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, with \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Suppose \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\), \(f^*\) is partly smooth at \(\bar v\) relative to \(M^*\), and \[\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f(\bar x),\qquad \bar x\in\operatorname{ri}\partial f^*(\bar v).\] If \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) and \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\), then for some \(K\), \[x_k\in M\quad\text{and}\quad v_k\in M^*\qquad(k\geq K).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nondegenerate convex conjugate pair, convergent primal-dual graph points eventually enter both the primal and dual active manifolds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(f^*\) are partly smooth relative to \(M\) and \(M^*\), respectively.
The primal and dual relative-interior conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in M\ \text{and}\ v_k\in M^*\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: symmetric application of primal and conjugate identification principles
simultaneous identification theorem requires source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Simultaneous primal and conjugate identification is nontrivial. A source is needed to verify that the stated convex partial-smoothness and relative-interior assumptions suffice for both eventual inclusions.

children.title: Algorithmic Active-Structure Identification Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Identification interfaces for projection, splitting, and Newton families.

children.title: Projection Identification
children.top_down_role: Active-structure detection through projection-based methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-manifold identification by metric projection onto a partly smooth set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset X\) be closed and prox-regular at \(\bar x\), and suppose its indicator \(\delta_C\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\)-manifold \(M\subset C\). Let \(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(\bar x)\), and choose \(\bar y=\bar x+\bar v\) in a neighborhood where \(P_C\) is single-valued. If \(y_k\to\bar y\), \[x_k=P_C(y_k),\qquad y_k-x_k\to\bar v,\] then \(x_k\to\bar x\), and there is \(K\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for every \(k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projections with residual normals converging to a relative-interior active normal eventually land on the active manifold of a prox-regular set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is closed and prox-regular at \(\bar x\).
\(\delta_C\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
\(\bar v\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(\bar x)\), and the projection is locally single-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to\bar x\) and \(\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in M\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection is the proximal mapping of a set indicator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection specialization is plausible, but an exact source is needed to confirm the prox-regular neighborhood, scaling of the reference normal, projection localization, and identification hypotheses.

children.title: Splitting Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification behavior in operator-splitting and proximal-splitting families.

knowledge_statements.title: Splitting Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-manifold identification by convergent forward–backward splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=h+g\) on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, where \(h\) is \(C^1\) with locally Lipschitz gradient and \(g\) is proper and lower semicontinuous. Suppose \(g\) is prox-regular, subdifferentially continuous, and partly smooth at a stationary point \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\), with \(-\nabla h(\bar x)\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(\bar x)\). For fixed admissible \(\gamma>0\), let \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}\bigl(x_k-\gamma\nabla h(x_k)\bigr).\] If \(x_k\to\bar x\), then there exists \(K\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for every \(k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent forward–backward iteration finitely identifies the active manifold when the limiting stationarity subgradient satisfies the relative-interior nondegeneracy condition.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) has locally Lipschitz gradient, and the proximal step for \(g\) is locally well-defined.
\(g\) is prox-regular, subdifferentially continuous, and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\).
\(-\nabla h(\bar x)\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(\bar x)\), and \(x_k\to\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in M\).

notation.meaning: smooth term of the composite objective

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: forward-backward residual supplies convergent subgradient pairs
exact admissible-step and identification theorem source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The phrase “fixed admissible” does not specify the step-size condition, and no theorem locator confirms the nonconvex proximal selection and identification hypotheses. These details materially affect the conclusion.

children.title: Active-Set Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite stabilization of active constraints, faces, supports, or strata.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification of an identifiable active manifold by convergent first-order iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), let \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), and let \(M\) be identifiable for \(\partial f\) at \((\bar x,\bar v)\). If an algorithm produces \(x_k\to\bar x\) and certificates \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) satisfying \(v_k\to\bar v\), then there exists \(K<\infty\) such that \(x_k\in M\) for every \(k\ge K\). Thus, when \(M\) encodes a support, sign pattern, or active constraints, that active set is constant and correct after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent iterates whose subgradient certificates approach a nondegenerate limiting certificate eventually enter, and thereafter remain on, the identifiable active manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x_k\in M\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf, but no source fixes the subdifferential and identifiability conventions. Under the attentive definition used elsewhere in the shard, convergence of f(x_k) to f(\bar x) is also required. Identification of M alone does not establish constancy of every listed combinatorial encoding without further assumptions.

children.title: Newton-Family Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification interfaces supporting local Newton-type models.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Family Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite manifold identification preceding a smooth Newton phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\), let \((\bar x,0)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), and let \(M\) be identifiable for \(F\) at \((\bar x,0)\). Suppose a Newton, semismooth-Newton, or quasi-Newton scheme produces \(x_k\to\bar x\) together with residual selections \(y_k\in F(x_k)\) such that \(y_k\to0\). Then \(x_k\in M\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). If the subsequent step is tangent to \(M\), the local iteration is a Newton-family method for the smooth reduced equation on \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual convergence forces Newton-family iterates onto the identifiable manifold; tangent steps then reduce the method to smooth Newton iteration on that manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ x_k\in M\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite membership follows from the stipulated mapping-identifiability definition, but the record applies this uniformly to Newton, semismooth-Newton, and quasi-Newton schemes without a source. Tangency alone is insufficient to conclude that the subsequent iteration is a smooth reduced Newton-family method.

children.title: Identifiable Surface-Graph Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Set and graph formulations of locally unavoidable active structure.

children.title: Identifiable Surfaces
children.top_down_role: Locally unavoidable surfaces associated with convergent variational information.

knowledge_statements.title: Identifiable Surfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential identification relative to a subgradient pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), let \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), and let \(M\subset\mathbb R^n\) contain \(\bar x\). The set \(M\) is identifiable for \(f\) at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) if every sequence \((x_k,v_k)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) satisfying \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\) and \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\) obeys \(x_k\in M\) eventually. It is an identifiable surface when, additionally, \(M\) is a smooth embedded manifold near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identifiable surface contains every sufficiently advanced base point of any nearby convergent subgradient sequence approaching the reference pair and function value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,v_k,f(x_k))\to(\bar x,\bar v,f(\bar x))\Rightarrow x_k\in M\text{ eventually}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf and the sequential statement is coherent, but identifiable-set definitions differ over subdifferential choice and whether function-value convergence is required. An authoritative source is needed to select the intended convention.

children.title: Identifiable Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph-based representations of locally unavoidable active structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Identifiable Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local graph concentration for a set-valued mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) be a set-valued mapping between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\), and let \(G\subset\operatorname{gph}F\) contain \((\bar x,\bar y)\). The subset \(G\) is an identifiable graph for \(F\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if every sequence \((x_k,y_k)\in\operatorname{gph}F\) converging to \((\bar x,\bar y)\) belongs to \(G\) eventually. Equivalently, there is a neighborhood \(W\) of \((\bar x,\bar y)\) such that \(\operatorname{gph}F\cap W\subset G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identifiable graph contains the entire graph of a set-valued mapping in some neighborhood of the reference graph point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists W\ni(\bar x,\bar y):\ \operatorname{gph}F\cap W\subset G\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential and neighborhood formulations are equivalent in finite-dimensional metric spaces, but no source establishes that this local graph-germ condition is the intended meaning of “identifiable graph” in this taxonomy.

children.title: Surface–Graph Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Translation between primal surface descriptions and graphical variational descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Surface–Graph Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between base-space identification and local subdifferential-graph concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), let \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}\partial f\), and let \(M\) contain \(\bar x\). Define \(G_M:=\operatorname{gph}\partial f\cap(M\times\mathbb R^n)\). Then \(M\) is identifiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\) precisely when every graph sequence converging to \((\bar x,\bar v)\), subject to any required function-value convergence, eventually lies in \(G_M\). Equivalently, in the non-attentive version, there exists a neighborhood \(W\) of \((\bar x,\bar v)\) satisfying \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\cap W\subset G_M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surface is identifiable exactly when the nearby relevant subdifferential graph is concentrated over that surface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ identifiable}\Longleftrightarrow G_M\text{ contains every relevant nearby graph sequence}\)

notation.meaning: portion of the subdifferential graph lying over the surface
neighborhood of the reference graph point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the correspondence leaf, but the statement combines attentive and non-attentive notions. Function-value-attentive identification generally corresponds to concentration of an attentive graph rather than the unrestricted local inclusion displayed here.

children.title: Post-Identification Geometry
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of remaining on the active manifold.

children.title: Smooth Reduced Models
children.top_down_role: Reduction to smooth manifold geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Reduced Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a partly smooth objective to its active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) embedded manifold \(M\), and choose a local \(C^2\) parametrization \(\phi:U\subset\mathbb R^d\to M\) with \(\phi(0)=\bar x\). The reduced objective is \(\widehat f:=f\circ\phi\). Partial smoothness implies that \(\widehat f\) is \(C^2\) near \(0\). After identification of \(M\), local optimization of \(f\) is represented by smooth optimization of \(\widehat f\), with tangent gradient determined by \(\nabla\widehat f(u)=D\phi(u)^*\nabla_M f(\phi(u))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once the active manifold is identified, a local parametrization converts the nonsmooth objective into a smooth reduced objective in manifold coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(f\text{ is partly smooth at }\bar x\text{ relative to }M\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat f=f\circ\phi\in C^2(U)\)

notation.meaning: local parametrization of the active manifold
Riemannian gradient of the manifold restriction

source_refs.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

source_witnesses.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the topic, but the cited smooth-manifold section does not directly support the partial-smoothness reduction claim. The coordinate-gradient identity also requires explicit Euclidean/Riemannian metric and adjoint conventions.

children.title: Post-Identification Rate-Newton Interface
children.top_down_role: Transition to faster local models after identification.

children.title: Post-Identification Local Rates
children.top_down_role: Local convergence regimes available after active geometry stabilizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Identification Local Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear rate inherited from a differentiable reduced fixed-point map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be identified after iteration \(K\), and suppose local coordinates \(u_k\) satisfy \(u_{k+1}=T(u_k)\), where \(T\) is continuously differentiable near a fixed point \(\bar u\). If \(\|DT(\bar u)\|=q<1\), then for every \(\varepsilon>0\) with \(q+\varepsilon<1\), all sufficiently large \(k\) satisfy \(\|u_{k+1}-\bar u\|\le(q+\varepsilon)\|u_k-\bar u\|\). Hence the identified iteration converges locally Q-linearly. If instead \(DT(\bar u)=0\) and \(DT\) is locally Lipschitz, the convergence is locally Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identification, contraction of the reduced derivative gives linear convergence; a vanishing Lipschitz derivative gives quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|u_{k+1}-\bar u\|}{\|u_k-\bar u\|}\le\|DT(\bar u)\|<1\)

notation.meaning: local manifold coordinates of the iterates

source_refs.locator: 6.5 Local Analysis p. 571

source_witnesses.locator: 6.5 Local Analysis p. 571

children.title: Reduced Newton Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Newton-type local models posed on identified smooth structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Newton Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration for the stationarity equation restricted to the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an identified \(C^2\) manifold \(M\), a point \(x_k\in M\), and the smooth restriction \(f_M=f|_M\). Compute the Riemannian gradient \(g_k=\nabla_M f(x_k)\) and Hessian \(H_k=\operatorname{Hess}_M f(x_k)\). If \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise solve \(H_kp_k=-g_k\) for \(p_k\in T_M(x_k)\), choose an accepted step length \(\alpha_k>0\), and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_kp_k)\), where \(R\) is a local retraction. Repeat until the gradient tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the Newton equation in the active tangent space and retract the step onto the identified manifold until the reduced gradient is small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla_M f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon\text{ at termination}\)

notation.meaning: tangent space to the active manifold
Riemannian Hessian of the reduced objective

source_refs.locator: 5.8 A Damped-Newton Method p. 448

source_witnesses.locator: 5.8 A Damped-Newton Method p. 448

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind, but the LCP damped-Newton locator does not establish this Riemannian active-manifold algorithm. “Accepted step length” is undefined, and solvability of the Newton equation needs a precise Hessian condition or a specified fallback.

children.title: Rate–Geometry Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Dependence of local rate behavior on identified curvature, regularity, and rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate–Geometry Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric conditions needed for fast reduced local convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an identified solution \(\bar x\in M\), rate–geometry compatibility holds when the algorithmic steps are asymptotically tangent, \(\operatorname{dist}(p_k,T_M(x_k))=o(\|p_k\|)\), the chosen retraction satisfies \(R_x(0)=x\) and \(DR_x(0)=\operatorname{id}_{T_M(x)}\), and the reduced Hessian \(\operatorname{Hess}_M f(\bar x):T_M(\bar x)\to T_M(\bar x)\) is nonsingular. Under these conditions, ambient nonsmooth geometry introduces no first-order error into the reduced Newton model; standard superlinear or quadratic rates apply when the corresponding Hessian-approximation and regularity conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fast local rates are compatible with identification when steps are tangent, retraction is first-order accurate, and the reduced Hessian is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(p_k,T_M(x_k))=o(\|p_k\|),\ DR_x(0)=\operatorname{id},\ \operatorname{Hess}_M f(\bar x)\text{ nonsingular}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the leaf, but the asserted superlinear or quadratic consequence is method-dependent and unsupported. Tangency, a first-order retraction, and Hessian nonsingularity alone do not supply all approximation, smoothness, globalization, and retraction-order hypotheses needed for those rates.

children.title: Sensitivity on Active Manifolds
children.top_down_role: Perturbation analysis along stable active structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sensitivity on Active Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit-function sensitivity of a stable reduced stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a \(C^2\) active manifold stable under parameters \(p\) near \(\bar p\), and let \(F_M(x,p)\in T_M(x)\) be a \(C^1\) reduced stationarity mapping with \(F_M(\bar x,\bar p)=0\). If the derivative \(D_xF_M(\bar x,\bar p):T_M(\bar x)\to T_M(\bar x)\) is invertible, then neighborhoods of \(\bar p\) and \(\bar x\) admit a unique \(C^1\) solution mapping \(x(p)\in M\). Its derivative is determined by \(Dx(\bar p)=-D_xF_M(\bar x,\bar p)^{-1}D_pF_M(\bar x,\bar p)\), in compatible local coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible reduced stationarity derivative yields a unique differentiable solution path along the stable active manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!\,x(\cdot)\in C^1:\ F_M(x(p),p)=0\)

notation.meaning: local solution mapping on the active manifold

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Smooth Calculus p. 1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the topic, but the cited introductory smooth-calculus section does not support the active-manifold stability claim. Because F_M takes values in varying tangent spaces, its derivative and inverse formula require a chart or bundle trivialization; the parameter domain is also not introduced.

children.title: Partial-Smoothness Calculus
children.top_down_role: Preservation of active geometry under common structural operations.

children.title: Partial-Smoothness Aggregation-Composition Calculus
children.top_down_role: Propagation of partial smoothness through aggregation and composition.

children.title: Sum Calculus
children.top_down_role: Partial-smoothness behavior under finite aggregation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial smoothness of a finite sum under manifold transversality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,r\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be prox-regular and partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M_i\). Assume subdifferential continuity at compatible reference subgradients and the transversality condition \(\sum_{i=1}^r z_i=0\), with \(z_i\in N_{M_i}(\bar x)\), implies \(z_i=0\) for every \(i\). Then \(M:=\bigcap_{i=1}^rM_i\) is a \(C^2\) manifold near \(\bar x\), and \(f:=\sum_{i=1}^rf_i\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M\), provided the exact subdifferential sum rule holds locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transversal intersection of active manifolds supports partial smoothness of the sum when the local exact subdifferential sum rule is valid.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i\text{ is prox-regular and partly smooth relative to }M_i\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^r f_i\text{ is partly smooth at }\bar x\text{ relative to }\bigcap_{i=1}^rM_i\)

children.title: Composition Calculus
children.top_down_role: Partial-smoothness behavior under smooth or structured composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pullback of partial smoothness through a smooth transversal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be prox-regular and partly smooth at \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\) relative to a \(C^2\) manifold \(M\), and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be \(C^2\). Assume the transversality condition \(N_M(\bar y)\cap\ker DF(\bar x)^*=\{0\}\) and a local exact chain rule \(\partial(h\circ F)(x)=DF(x)^*\partial h(F(x))\). Then \(F^{-1}(M)\) is a \(C^2\) manifold near \(\bar x\), and \(h\circ F\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(F^{-1}(M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth map pulls back a partly smooth function and its active manifold when transversality and the exact subdifferential chain rule hold.
assumptions_latex: \(h\text{ is prox-regular and partly smooth at }F(\bar x)\text{ relative to }M\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h\circ F\text{ is partly smooth at }\bar x\text{ relative to }F^{-1}(M)\)

notation.meaning: active manifold of the outer function

children.title: Qualification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Compatibility failures that obstruct sum or composition transfer.

knowledge_statements.title: Qualification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for transversality in sum and smooth-preimage partial-smoothness calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1,M_2\subset E\) be active \(C^2\) manifolds through \(\bar x\), and let \(F:E\to Y\) be \(C^1\) with \(F(\bar x)\in M\subset Y\). Sum calculus is qualified when \(N_{M_1}(\bar x)\cap[-N_{M_2}(\bar x)]=\{0\}\). Composition through the preimage \(F^{-1}(M)\) is qualified when \(N_M(F(\bar x))\cap\ker DF(\bar x)^*=\{0\}\). The qualification boundary consists of data for which the corresponding intersection contains a nonzero normal; there the expected active intersection or preimage may fail to be a smooth manifold of the predicted dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualification fails when active manifolds have opposing nonzero normals or a nonzero outer normal is annihilated by the composition derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{M_1}(\bar x)\cap[-N_{M_2}(\bar x)]\ne\{0\}\) or \(N_M(F(\bar x))\cap\ker DF(\bar x)^*\ne\{0\}\) marks the relevant qualification boundary.

notation.meaning: normal space to the smooth manifold M at z
adjoint of the derivative of F at the reference point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the qualification-boundary leaf, and the displayed normal-intersection tests are plausible finite-dimensional transversality conditions. No citation supports their use as the exact sum and preimage qualifications for partial-smoothness calculus, and the ambient assumptions on E and Y are unstated.

children.title: Spectral Partial Smoothness
children.top_down_role: Active eigenspace and rank structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Partial Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral lifting for real symmetric matrices with eigenvalue multiplicities retained by the active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be permutation-invariant and partly smooth at \(\lambda(\bar X)\) relative to a permutation-compatible \(C^2\) manifold \(m\). Define \(H(X)=h(\lambda(X))\) on the real symmetric matrices. If the multiplicity pattern of \(\bar X\) is compatible with \(m\), then \(H\) is partly smooth at \(\bar X\) relative to the spectral lift \(\mathcal M=\{U\operatorname{Diag}(z)U^\top:z\in m,\ U\text{ orthogonal}\}\) locally restricted to that multiplicity pattern. Its tangent and normal geometry are invariant under orthogonal conjugation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial smoothness of a symmetric eigenvalue function lifts to a matrix manifold encoding the active eigenvalue multiplicities and eigenspaces.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is permutation-invariant and partly smooth at \(\lambda(\bar X)\) relative to \(m\).
The local eigenvalue multiplicity pattern is compatible with \(m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=h\circ\lambda\) is partly smooth at \(\bar X\) relative to the local spectral lift \(\mathcal M\).

notation.meaning: eigenvalue vector of a real symmetric matrix, in fixed order
spectral active manifold lifted from the eigenvalue manifold

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits a spectral lifting claim, but the meanings of permutation compatibility and multiplicity compatibility are not precise enough to verify that the displayed lift is locally a C2 manifold or that partial smoothness transfers. An authoritative spectral partial-smoothness theorem with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized gradient and simple-eigenvalue differentiability of a spectral maximum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral generalized differentiation at a point where the leading eigenvalue has multiplicity r.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the source-defined spectral setting, f is Lipschitz and regular at x, and
\[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\left\{\left[\langle U^*A'_1Uw,w\rangle,\ldots,\langle U^*A'_mUw,w\rangle\right]:w\in S_r\right\}.\]
If the leading eigenvalue \(\lambda_1\) has multiplicity one, then f is differentiable at x and, for every i,
\[\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)=\left(U^*\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_i}(x)U\right)_{11}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the stated spectral setting, f is Lipschitz and regular at x, and its generalized gradient is the convex hull of the quadratic-form vectors generated by unit vectors in the leading eigenspace. If the leading eigenvalue is simple, f is differentiable and each partial derivative is the (1,1)-entry of the corresponding matrix derivative expressed in the U basis.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ and the objects }f,A,U,S_r,\lambda_1\text{ are as defined in the source's spectral setup}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz and regular at }x;\quad \partial f(x)=\operatorname{co}\{[\langle U^*A'_1Uw,w\rangle,\ldots,\langle U^*A'_mUw,w\rangle]:w\in S_r\};\quad r=1\Rightarrow \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)=\left(U^*\frac{\partial A}{\partial x_i}(x)U\right)_{11}.

children.title: Primal–Dual Partial Smoothness
children.top_down_role: Coupled active structures in saddle and primal-dual systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Partial Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product active geometry for a standard convex–concave saddle system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Ax,y\rangle-g^*(y)\), where \(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions. If \(f\) is partly smooth at \(\bar x\) relative to \(M_x\) and \(g^*\) is partly smooth at \(\bar y\) relative to \(M_y\), then the nonsmooth primal–dual geometry is carried by \(M_x\times M_y\). The saddle subdifferential mapping satisfies \(\partial_xL(x,y)=\partial f(x)+A^*y\) and \(-\partial_yL(x,y)=\partial g^*(y)-Ax\); the bilinear coupling shifts the subgradients without changing their parallel spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partly smooth primal and dual terms induce a product active manifold; linear coupling translates their subgradients but preserves active tangent geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g^*\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(f\) and \(g^*\) are partly smooth relative to \(M_x\) and \(M_y\) at the reference pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled active structure is \(M_x\times M_y\), with the displayed translated primal and dual subdifferentials.

notation.meaning: adjoint of the linear coupling operator A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role is reasonable for this topic, and the two subdifferential identities are standard. However, the spaces and domain of A are not introduced, and no source establishes the stronger assertion that the coupled active geometry is precisely the product manifold under the stated hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection representation and semismoothness of the KKT residual operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-based function-space KKT residual under the stated decomposition of the control derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the projection-based regularity assumptions, \[\Pi(y,u,w)(\omega)=u(\omega)-P_C\!\left(-\lambda^{-1}G(y,u,w)(\omega)\right).\] The operator \(\Sigma:Y\times L^r(\Omega)^m\times W^*\to Y^*\times L^r(\Omega)^m\times W\) is locally Lipschitz and \(\partial_C\Sigma\)-semismooth. Every \(M\in\partial_C\Sigma(y,u,w)\) has the form \[M=\begin{pmatrix}L_{yy}&L_{yu}&E_y^*\\\lambda^{-1}DG_y&I+\lambda^{-1}DG_u&\lambda^{-1}DG_w\\E_y&E_u&0\end{pmatrix},\] where \(D\in L^\infty(\Omega)^{m\times m}\) and \(D(\omega)\in\partial_C P_C(-\lambda^{-1}G(y,u,w)(\omega))\) almost everywhere on \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the projection-based assumptions, the complementarity component is the control minus the projection of −G/λ. The resulting KKT residual is locally Lipschitz and semismooth, with generalized derivatives given by the stated block operator involving a pointwise generalized derivative of the projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi(y,u,w)=u-P_C(-\lambda^{-1}G(y,u,w)),\quad \Sigma\text{ is locally Lipschitz and }\partial_C\Sigma\text{-semismooth, with the displayed generalized derivative family.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection-based regularity assumptions for a semismooth KKT operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-space KKT systems with a strongly monotone control term and a semismooth metric projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist \(1\le r<p'\le\infty\) such that \(E:Y\times L^r(\Omega)^m\to W\) and \(J:Y\times L^r(\Omega)^m\to\mathbb R\) are twice continuously differentiable, and \(L_u(y,u,w)=\lambda u+G(y,u,w)\) for some \(\lambda>0\). The map \(G:Y\times L^r(\Omega)^m\times W^*\to L^r(\Omega)^m\) is continuously Fréchet differentiable and is locally Lipschitz when regarded as taking values in \(L^{p'}(\Omega)^m\). Moreover, \(\pi(x_1,x_2)=x_1-P_C(x_1-\lambda^{-1}x_2)\), where \(P_C\) is semismooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume twice differentiability of E and J, a decomposition of the control derivative into λu plus a smooth remainder G with stronger local Lipschitz integrability, and a semismooth projection-based complementarity map.
assumptions_latex: G:Y\times L^r(\Omega)^m\times W^*\to L^r(\Omega)^m\text{ is continuously Fréchet differentiable}
G\text{ is locally Lipschitz as a map into }L^{p'}(\Omega)^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These conditions define the projection-based regularity regime for the associated KKT residual operator.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semismoothness and generalized derivative of the KKT residual operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT residual operator under the stated function-space regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the preceding regularity assumptions, \(\Sigma:Y\times L^p(\Omega)^m\times W^*\to Y^*\times L^r(\Omega)^m\times W\) is locally Lipschitz and \(\partial_C\Sigma\)-semismooth, with \(\partial_C\Sigma=\{L_v'\}\times\partial_C^\circ\Pi\times\{E'\}\). Every \(M\in\partial_C\Sigma(y,u,w)\) has the form \[M=\begin{pmatrix}L_{yy}&L_{yu}&E_y^*\\D_2L_{uy}&D_1I+D_2L_{uu}&D_2E_u^*\\E_y&E_u&0\end{pmatrix},\] where \(D_i\in L^\infty(\Omega)^{m\times m}\) and \((D_1\mid D_2)(\omega)\in\partial_C\pi(u(\omega),L_u(y,u,w)(\omega))\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated regularity assumptions, the function-space KKT residual operator is locally Lipschitz and semismooth. Its generalized derivatives are block KKT operators whose middle row is determined pointwise by a generalized derivative of π.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Sigma\text{ is locally Lipschitz and }\partial_C\Sigma\text{-semismooth, with the displayed characterization of }\partial_C\Sigma(y,u,w).

children.title: Identification Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degeneracies preventing finite or stable active-structure identification.

children.title: Active-Structure Branching Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Competing manifolds or strata near the reference point.

children.title: Nonunique Active Structures
children.top_down_role: Competing active manifolds or strata compatible with the same reference geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Active Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local failure of uniqueness for candidate identifying manifolds or strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak A(\bar x,\bar v)\) denote the collection of admissible active \(C^2\) manifold germs associated with \((\bar x,\bar v)\), where \(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\). The active structure is nonunique when there exist \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak A(\bar x,\bar v)\) such that every neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) satisfies \(M_1\cap U\ne M_2\cap U\). In this regime, convergence of iterates and subgradients to \((\bar x,\bar v)\) alone cannot specify which manifold germ must be identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active structure is nonunique when two genuinely different local manifold germs satisfy the admissibility requirements at the same point-subgradient pair.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak A(\bar x,\bar v)\) is the prescribed family of admissible active manifold germs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathfrak A(\bar x,\bar v)/{\sim}_{\mathrm{germ}}|>1\) prevents unique active-manifold identification from local limit data alone.

notation.meaning: family of admissible active manifold germs
equality of manifolds on some neighborhood of the reference point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role matches the leaf. The mathematical force of the statement depends entirely on the unspecified admissibility requirements defining the family of manifold germs, so the nonuniqueness and identification consequence cannot be verified without a cited framework.

children.title: Branching Active Structures
children.top_down_role: Local active pieces that split into multiple incident geometric branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Active Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A maximum of smooth pieces exhibits distinct active branches meeting at a switching stratum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x_1,x_2)=\max\{x_1,x_2\}\), the regions \(B_1=\{x:x_1>x_2\}\) and \(B_2=\{x:x_2>x_1\}\) are smooth branches on which \(f\) equals different affine functions, while \(S=\{x:x_1=x_2\}\) is their switching stratum. Sequences approaching any \(\bar x\in S\) from \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) have active index sets \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2\}\), respectively, whereas the limiting active index set is \(\{1,2\}\). Thus no single branch represents all nearby approaches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of two coordinates has two smooth branches meeting on a tie line, and different approach directions select different active indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approaches to \(S\) from \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) select incompatible singleton active sets.

notation.meaning: open region on which the ith affine piece is uniquely active
switching stratum where both pieces are active

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the branching leaf, and the active-index calculations for the maximum of two coordinates are directly correct. A specific source or explicit standard-field rationale is still required to support its interpretation as an active-structure identification failure example.

children.title: Branch-Selection Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of the selected active branch to perturbations or approach directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Selection Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrarily small perturbations reverse the selected smooth branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f_\varepsilon(x_1,x_2)=\max\{x_1+\varepsilon,x_2-\varepsilon\}\). At \(x=(0,0)\), the first affine branch is uniquely active for \(\varepsilon>0\), the second is uniquely active for \(\varepsilon<0\), and both are active for \(\varepsilon=0\). Hence perturbations with arbitrarily small norm and opposite signs select different active branches, although \(f_\varepsilon\) converges uniformly to \(f_0\) on \(\mathbb R^2\). Branch selection is therefore discontinuous at the unperturbed tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small signed perturbation of a two-piece maximum switches the uniquely active branch at the same reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active-branch selector at \(x=0\) is discontinuous as \(\varepsilon\to0\).

notation.meaning: scalar perturbation controlling which affine branch dominates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the leaf. The branch selections and global uniform convergence follow from the displayed formula, but the record supplies neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale for the claimed branch-selection instability boundary.

children.title: Degenerate Normal Geometry
children.top_down_role: Insufficient transverse separation for stable identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Normal Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of transverse separation between competing active manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1,M_2\subset E\) be candidate active \(C^2\) manifolds through \(\bar x\). Their normal geometry is degenerate at \(\bar x\) when \(N_{M_1}(\bar x)\cap[-N_{M_2}(\bar x)]\ne\{0\}\). Equivalently, there is a nonzero vector normal to \(M_1\) whose negative is normal to \(M_2\). This abnormal normal prevents transverse intersection; consequently, the intersection may have an unstable dimension and small perturbations need not preserve the local active geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal geometry is degenerate when competing active manifolds possess opposing nonzero normals, so their intersection is not transverse.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are embedded \(C^2\) manifolds through \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{M_1}(\bar x)\cap[-N_{M_2}(\bar x)]\ne\{0\}\) characterizes failure of transversality.

notation.meaning: normal space to M at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits degenerate normal geometry, and the normal-space intersection is the standard failure of transversality for two smooth manifolds. The claims about unstable dimension and perturbation behavior require a specific manifold-transversality or variational-analysis source.

children.title: Identification Robustness Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Repeated switching or loss of finite identification under persistent perturbations.

children.title: Vanishing Identification Margins
children.top_down_role: Loss of geometric separation needed for stable active-structure detection.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Identification Margins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collapse of strict-complementarity distance along an identifying sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex and let \((x_k,v_k)\to(\bar x,\bar v)\) with \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). Define the identification margin by \(\delta_k=\operatorname{dist}(v_k,\operatorname{rbd}\partial f(x_k))\), measured within \(\operatorname{aff}\partial f(x_k)\). Identification margins vanish when \(\delta_k\to0\). Then the subgradients approach the relative boundary of their admissible faces, so no uniform positive perturbation radius can keep all sufficiently large \(v_k\) in the corresponding relative interiors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identification margins vanish when subgradients approach the relative boundaries of their subdifferential faces, eliminating any uniform strict-complementarity buffer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_k\to0\) implies that no uniform radius protects the relative-interior membership of all large-index subgradients.

notation.meaning: relative boundary of a convex set C
distance from the kth subgradient to the relative boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role fits the leaf. The distance construction is plausible, but its interpretation as an identification margin across subdifferentials with potentially varying affine hulls, and the resulting uniform-perturbation conclusion, require a cited identification theorem or robustness framework.

children.title: Active-Set Chattering
children.top_down_role: Repeated switching among competing active pieces near a reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Chattering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite switching among active labels near a limiting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)\) be a finite-valued active-set mapping and let \(x_k\to\bar x\). The sequence chatters when \(A(x_{k+1})\ne A(x_k)\) for infinitely many indices \(k\). Equivalently, the active-set sequence is not eventually constant. When two or more values of \(A\) occur infinitely often, no finite iteration identifies a single active set, even though the primal iterates converge to the same limiting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set chattering is infinite switching of active labels along a convergent sequence, preventing finite identification.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) maps nearby points into a finite family of active sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infinitely many changes in \(A(x_k)\) preclude eventual active-set identification.

notation.meaning: active index set assigned to x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role fits this terminal container, and infinite changes are equivalent to failure of eventual constancy for the displayed sequence. The record nevertheless has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale establishing this as the intended active-set chattering notion.

children.title: Persistent Identification Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Residual perturbations that prevent finite stabilization of active geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Identification Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence without eventual membership in the target active manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be the target active manifold through \(\bar x\), and let \(x_k\to\bar x\). Identification is persistently inexact when, for every \(K\), there exists \(k\ge K\) such that \(x_k\notin M\). Thus the iterates may approach \(M\), with \(\operatorname{dist}(x_k,M)\to0\), while never attaining permanent manifold membership. If approximate subgradient errors remain comparable to or larger than the available identification margin, this behavior is not excluded by convergence alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identification remains inexact when convergent iterates fail to lie on the target manifold eventually, even if their distance to it vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is an embedded active manifold containing \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall K\,\exists k\ge K:\ x_k\notin M\) is failure of finite exact identification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role fits the leaf, and the quantified condition correctly negates eventual membership in M. The additional assertion connecting persistent inexactness to subgradient errors and identification margins is not formalized or supported by a source.

children.title: Robustness Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Perturbation regimes separating stable identification from persistent failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-interior margin as a sharp local perturbation threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex set, let \(v\in\operatorname{ri}C\), and define \(\delta=\operatorname{dist}(v,\operatorname{rbd}C)>0\), with distance computed in \(\operatorname{aff}C\). For every perturbation \(e\in\operatorname{par}C\) satisfying \(\|e\|<\delta\), one has \(v+e\in\operatorname{ri}C\). Hence \(\delta\) is a certified robustness radius for preserving the relative-interior condition used in active-structure identification; no larger universal radius follows from this distance alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a convex set’s relative boundary gives a perturbation threshold that preserves relative-interior membership and its identification condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\in\operatorname{par}C\) and \(\|e\|<\delta\) imply \(v+e\in\operatorname{ri}C\).

notation.meaning: linear space parallel to the affine hull of C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-interior ball statement is plausible convex geometry, but a certificate or condition may fit this threshold leaf more exactly than property. A source is required both for the relative-boundary radius statement and for the asserted sharpness that no larger universal radius follows from the distance alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise KL Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property localized at one finite-valued reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property at \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), a number \(\eta>0\), and a concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb R_+\), continuous at \(0\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\), \(\varphi\in C^1(0,\eta)\), and \(\varphi'>0\), such that \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\) whenever \(x\in U\) and \(f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise KL property bounds the reciprocal subgradient slope by a local concave desingularizing derivative near one reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed desingularized slope inequality holds locally above the value \(f(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential of f at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role exactly fits the pointwise KL leaf, and the formula resembles the standard limiting-subdifferential KL property. The record does not specify that E is an appropriate finite-dimensional Euclidean space and provides no authoritative definition with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz Property and Exponent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the local KL property through the limiting-subdifferential residual, including the power-type exponent convention and semialgebraic sufficient regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower semicontinuous function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ satisfies the KL property at $\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}(\partial f)$ if there exist $\alpha,\delta>0$ and a continuous concave function $\phi:[0,\alpha)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ such that $\phi(0)=0$, $\phi\in C^1(0,\alpha)$, $\phi'(s)>0$ for all $s\in(0,\alpha)$, and, for every $x\in\mathbb B(\bar x;\delta)$ satisfying $f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\alpha$, $$\phi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\geq1.$$ If $\phi(s)=\gamma s^{1-\beta}$ for some $\gamma>0$ and $\beta\in[0,1)$, then $f$ has KL exponent $\beta$ at $\bar x$. Every proper closed semialgebraic function satisfies the KL property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper lower semicontinuous function has the pointwise KL property when a concave desingularizing function makes the local subdifferential residual satisfy the stated lower bound. A power desingularizer defines the KL exponent. Proper closed semialgebraic functions satisfy the KL property.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper and lower semicontinuous}

knowledge_statements.title: Slope KL Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL inequalities expressed through a selected subdifferential slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), and set \(\bar f=f(\bar x)\). For a chosen subdifferential \(\mathcal Df\), define its slope by \(s_{\mathcal D}(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\mathcal Df(x))\). The associated slope KL variant holds at \(\bar x\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\), \(\eta>0\), and a concave desingularizing function \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'>0\) such that \[\varphi'(f(x)-\bar f)s_{\mathcal D}(x)\ge1\] for all \(x\in U\) satisfying \(0<f(x)-\bar f<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A slope KL variant replaces the usual limiting-subdifferential norm by the distance to a specified subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Df\) is a specified subdifferential mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))s_{\mathcal D}(x)\ge1\) locally above the reference level.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract Set-Valued-Mapping KL Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-residual KL variant obtained by replacing the limiting subdifferential with an abstract multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal F:\mathbb{R}^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^n$. Given $\bar x$, $\alpha,\delta>0$, and a KL function $\phi$, the abstract mapping KL condition requires that, for every $x\in\mathbb B(\bar x;\delta)$ satisfying $f(\bar x)<f(x)<f(\bar x)+\alpha$, $$\phi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\mathcal F(x))\ge1.$$ Consequently, $\mathcal F(x)\ne\varnothing$ throughout this punctured local value neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Variant Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coincidence of metric and subdifferential KL formulations under regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. At every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), the descending metric slope satisfies \[|\nabla f|(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)).\] Consequently, at any \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), the metric KL inequality and the convex-subdifferential slope KL inequality are equivalent with the same neighborhood, value window, and desingularizing function. The same equality, with \(\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\), holds locally for continuously differentiable functions on finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex functions, and locally for smooth functions, metric slope and subdifferential slope coincide, so their KL formulations are identical.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a Hilbert space; or \(f\) is continuously differentiable in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\nabla f|(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\), hence the corresponding KL variants are equivalent.
review_flags: Exact source locators for both the convex and smooth slope identities are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex and continuously differentiable slope identities are plausible standard results, but the record combines two regimes without any locator supporting either identity or the resulting KL equivalence. Exact sources are required before the theorem can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Variant Separation Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Variant Separation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of regularity separates metric, limiting, and Clarke slope quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equality between metric and generalized-gradient slopes need not survive outside convex or subdifferentially regular regimes. For \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) defined by \(f(x)=-|x|\), the descending metric slope at the origin is \[|\nabla f|(0)=1,\] whereas the Clarke subdifferential is \(\partial^{\mathrm C}f(0)=[-1,1]\), so \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial^{\mathrm C}f(0))=0.\] Thus replacing the metric slope by the Clarke subdifferential distance can change a positive descent measure into zero; equivalence of the associated KL inequalities requires additional regularity and cannot be asserted for arbitrary locally Lipschitz functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the nonsmooth local maximum −|x|, metric slope is one but Clarke slope is zero, demonstrating failure of unrestricted variant equivalence.
assumptions_latex: The generalized-gradient variant uses the Clarke subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\nabla f|(0)=1\ne0=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial^{\mathrm C}f(0))\).
review_flags: The computation is elementary, but an authoritative locator for the comparison framework is absent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed counterexample computation is mathematically consistent and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no authoritative locator is supplied for the metric-slope and Clarke-slope comparison framework.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}\) be real analytic on an open set \(U\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\bar x\in U\) satisfy \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\). Then there exist a neighborhood \(V\subset U\) of \(\bar x\), constants \(C>0\) and \(\theta\in[1/2,1)\), such that \[|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^{\theta}\le C\|\nabla f(x)\|\qquad(x\in V).\] Hence, on the region where \(f(x)>f(\bar x)\), the analytic function has the KL property at \(\bar x\) with a power-type desingularizing function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-dimensional real-analytic function satisfies a local gradient inequality with an exponent between one half and one, and therefore a power-type KL inequality, at each critical point.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that, near \(\bar x\), a differentiable function \(f\) satisfies the classical gradient inequality \[|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^{\theta}\le C\|\nabla f(x)\|\] for constants \(C>0\) and \(\theta\in[1/2,1)\). Define \(\varphi(s)=C(1-\theta)^{-1}s^{1-\theta}\) for \(s\ge0\). Since \(\varphi'(s)=Cs^{-\theta}\) for \(s>0\), the gradient inequality on \(f(x)>f(\bar x)\) is represented as \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\|\nabla f(x)\|\ge1.\] Thus the classical exponent \(\theta\) corresponds to the KL desingularizing exponent \(1-\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical gradient inequality is represented in KL form by a power desingularizer proportional to s raised to one minus the gradient exponent.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and assume that constants \(C>0\) and \(\theta\in[1/2,1)\) satisfy \[|f(x)-f(\bar x)|^{\theta}\le C\|\nabla f(x)\|\] for every \(x\in U\). Define \(\varphi(s)=C(1-\theta)^{-1}s^{1-\theta}\), and choose \(\eta>0\). Then every \(x\in U\) with \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\) satisfies \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1,\] because \(\partial f(x)=\{\nabla f(x)\}\). Therefore every real-analytic function covered by the classical gradient inequality has the KL property locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable function, substituting the power desingularizer and identifying the limiting subdifferential with the gradient singleton converts the classical gradient inequality into KL form.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and subanalytic. Assume that \(\operatorname{dom}f\) is closed and that \(f\) is continuous on \(\operatorname{dom}f\). Then, at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\), there exist a neighborhood \(U\), a number \(\eta>0\), and a concave desingularizing function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\), continuous at \(0\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'(s)>0\) for \(s\in(0,\eta)\), such that \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\] whenever \(x\in U\) and \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper lower-semicontinuous subanalytic function with closed domain that is continuous on its domain has the KL property at each point where its limiting subdifferential is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subanalytic Zero-Set Łojasiewicz Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform power comparison for continuous subanalytic functions on a compact subanalytic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and subanalytic, and let \(\phi,\psi:S\to\mathbb R\) be continuous subanalytic functions. If \(\phi^{-1}(0)\subseteq\psi^{-1}(0)\), then there exist \(\rho>0\) and \(N^*\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) such that \(\rho|\psi(x)|^{N^*}\le |\phi(x)|\) for every \(x\in S\). If also \(\psi^{-1}(0)\subseteq\phi^{-1}(0)\), then there exist \(\rho_1,\rho_2>0\) and \(N_1,N_2\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\) such that \(\rho_1|\psi(x)|^{N_1}\le |\phi(x)|\le \rho_2|\psi(x)|^{1/N_2}\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inclusion of zero sets for two continuous subanalytic functions on a compact subanalytic domain gives a uniform one-sided power inequality. Equality of their zero sets gives a two-sided power comparison.
assumptions_latex: S\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact and subanalytic}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\rho>0,\ N^*\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\ \forall x\in S:\ \rho|\psi(x)|^{N^*}\le|\phi(x)|;\quad \psi^{-1}(0)\subseteq\phi^{-1}(0)\Rightarrow\text{the stated two-sided power comparison.}

knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic KL Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KL property for proper lower-semicontinuous semialgebraic functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and semialgebraic, meaning that its epigraph is a semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\). Then \(f\) has the KL property at every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}\partial f\): there exist a neighborhood \(U\), \(\eta>0\), and a concave function \(\varphi:[0,\eta)\to\mathbb{R}_+\), with \(\varphi(0)=0\) and \(\varphi'>0\), such that \[\varphi'(f(x)-f(\bar x))\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\ge1\] whenever \(x\in U\) and \(0<f(x)-f(\bar x)<\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper lower-semicontinuous semialgebraic function satisfies the KL inequality at each point where its limiting subdifferential is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has the KL property at \(\bar x\).
